LV1 is a large sword, with a large rectangular blunt blade similar to its original appereance, but it has no clear handguard.

LV2 gains an oversized handguard made of 1 red rectangle on each side, the blade gains a red part over the blade & the blade becomes car key shaped.

LV3 has the swords red parts on the handguard & on the blade being more detailed compared to LV2. The blade's point now is wheel shaped.

In addition to these 3, during Dragon Install the Fireseal turns into a sword shaped pillar of fire.

entries.name: Firewheel Mk.2
entries.content:
Firewheel Mk. II is a massive displacement motorcycle designed and developed by Sol Badguy himself. Much of the development was accomplished through his newly found magic that can materialize certain objects.

The derivation of the name is obvious—it is based on a servant he once summoned, the Fire Wheel.

entries.name: Flashing Fang
entries.content:
The Flashing Fang is one of the eight Sacred Treasures that comprise the Outrage and Sol's creation. It is a Magic Amplification device that channels and intensifies light magic, shaped akin to a lightbulb/funnel with an hourglass inside of it. It was previously located at Harden Fort and under the custody of the U.N. until Sol came to retrieve it in order to reassemble the Outrage.

After seeing the Gun Smith Dog recommended by Dr. Paradigm to help in the construction of the Junkyard Dog MK II casing, Sol was successfully able to merge the Fireseal with the Senga, creating the Junkyard Dog MK III.

entries.name: Goldlewis' coffin
entries.content:
Goldlewis Dickinson's coffin is a weapon in the Guilty Gear world. The coffin contains a mysterious entity, called a "cryptid" by Goldlewis himself, although it seems to be an extraterrestrial.

The large, six-sided coffin is of gothic design, made out of dark brown, wood-like material with metallic ornate designs and four door knocker-like rings on its sides. The ring on the top-right side has a large metal chain attached to it, which allows Goldlewis to swing it around and carry it on his shoulder. The coffin's top and bottom have nine blunt spikes, similar to a meat tenderizer. The lid has two silver spikes on each side, on which a sign reading 'AREA 51 - UNITED STATES' is bolted on, whilst an extra-terrestrial warning sign is stamped on.

Being hidden within the coffin, the only parts seen of the entity's body are its arms, which are lanky and seems to be composed of a luminous azure material.

he coffin itself seems to be extremely durable, since Goldlewis can create a crater on the ground by slamming. However, it strength lies on the powers held by the 'mysterious life-form' it contains. It is able to open the coffin's lid and assist Goldlewis with a single arm, or make multiple ones.

The seemingly-extraterrestrial entity is capable of providing Goldlewis with various items that far surpass the current technological level, and can materialize a gatling gun, aerial explosives, or even a rubber chicken. Another of its powers seem the ability to tamper with telecommunication, shown to be able to call Goldlewis and distract him whilst the defeated enemy is abducted.

entries.name: Johnny's katana
entries.content: Johnny's signature weapon is a katana. Johnny's sword is wooden at both the handle and the scabbard, while the blade itself is metal. Rather than fastening the sheath to his belt, Johnny carries his sword around by hand.

entries.name: Junkyard Dog
entries.content:
Junkyard Dog, also simply called Junkyard, is Sol Badguy's primary weapon, which combines two Sacred Treasures—the Fireseal and Flashing Fang. It can be used as blunt sword, and as a long-range cannon that can fire the Saint Oratorio spell.

The Junkyard Dog MK.3 borrows a similar but leaner shape from Order-Sol's MK.1. The MK.3 also consists of the Fireseal and the Flashing Fang, and can also fire the Saint Oratorio spell. This is also present in the Junkyard Dog MK.2. The MK.3 has the ability to open its casing, allowing for the loading and unloading of its "ammo". Its "cartridges" require "Ignition" by Sol, then loading onto the weapon.

In 2186, following the Baptisma 13 incident, Sol decides to prepare himself for the second coming of Valentine's forces, Sol decides to upgrade his Fireseal sword, and designs the Junkyard Dog as a simple version of the Outrage he himself created in 2073. Unfortunately, it requires the Flashing Fang in order to fulfill that function.

Sol, accompanied by Sin, thus embarks upon a journey to collect the Sacred Treasure and soon discovers that the Fang is being held under tight security inside a United Nations facility known as Harden Fort. Around July, 2187, Sol and Sin fight their way into the facility, where they run into Baldias. After a tremendous battle, Sol is able to defeat the Conclave member and take the Fang. With both treasures in his possession, Sol hires a dog-human gunsmith, who was introduced to him by Dr. Paradigm, to build the Junkyard.

Junkyard Dog can be used as a blunt weapon, or to fire projectiles. It is designed to be a simple version of the Outrage—a portable weapon that could fire the Saint Oratorio, a very high-energy spell that is extremely dangerous to the user.

By virtue of being composed of both the Fireseal and the Flashing Fang, it is able to concentrate and amplify fire magic, and create and manipulate light magic. It is a powerful weapon; at three-fold output, a blast of the Junkyard is able to "smash a mountain", according to Sol.

entries.name: Last Resort
entries.content:
Last Resort is powerful weapon that appears in Guilty Gear X Lightning the Argent, capable of killing Megadeath-class Gears. It is a magic particle-based satellite weapon that has a destruction radius of several kilometers: As seen with the Hydra, its radius was 3 kilometers (after 3,000 residents were evacuated).

Because Last Resort can reduce all life to nothing within its space during the blast, no one can enter the kill-zone.

The charge time requirement of the Satellite is roughly 2000 seconds per 1.5 kilometers, even so it has a terrible effect on the environment and ultimately makes the target area a blockaded zone (or No-Man’s Land) for several hundred years.

entries.name: Leo's twin blades
entries.content:
Unnamed twin blades are Leo Whitefang's signature weapons which he wields in all of his game appearances. They are versatile weapons that he is able to shapeshift.

Leo's twin blades can be described as greatswords that are shaped like large crosses. The blades are unique in that they possess handles on the sides of the crossguards so that they are wielded as long fist-weapons rather than as actual swords.

Using his twin blades, Leo can harness powerful energy that can be launched in waves (as shown through his moves Graviert Würde and Stahl Wirbel). Additionally, they also seem capable of rotating 360 degrees around his fists, as seen when he switches between his two main fighting stances. The blades can even rotate at high speeds, as seen when he is using Stahl Wirbel. When not engaged in combat, they've been shown to be capable of shrinking down to a portable size. Although not fully explored, it is shown that they can also take on alternate shapes, with Leo's Instant Kill being the prime example. In this Instant Kill the ends of the blades extend into the shapes of two-halves of a lion's maw, and are put together as he divebombs his opponent. It is unknown what types of magic the twin blades are currently able to harness, though it can be speculated that their shape-changing capabilities are a result of him using magic on them to take on the shapes he desires. Magic would also explain how he gets the blades to rotate without affecting his ability to slash wtih them.

entries.name: Magnolia Éclair
entries.content:
Magnolia Éclair is the name for two weapons in the Guilty Gear world, used by Ky Kiske as replacements for the Thunderseal. The first Magnolia Éclair is a rifle that he wields in Guilty Gear Vastedge XT, whereas Magnolia Éclair II is the sword he uses in the Xrd games.

The first Magnolia Éclair is the rifle-like weapon with a blue and white color scheme.

Magnolia Éclair II is a sword with a fine, delicate blade, and is balanced to be carried with one hand. "Magnolia Éclair II - Patented Nov, 20 , 21xx" and "Glory be to the Kingdom" are etched along the blade, and the scabbard bears the text "Tirana Fact Made in Trana, Illyria Since Apr, 1986".

entries.name: Marlene
entries.content:
Marlene is I-No's electric guitar that she uses as a weapon. I-No uses it in both magical and physical attacks strumming it to produce damaging sound waves or slamming it to her opponents. She also uses it for flight as she rides it like a witch's broom when she dashes in the air. Marlene is also listed among the things I-No likes in her profile.


Visual presentation-wise Marlene is an "almost-direct" replica of the Duesenberg Guitars company's "Starplayer TV" (also known as "Starplayer II") real-life guitar model, albeit made with reinforced materials (such as titanium and space flight-grade duraluminium) to withstand heavy impacts such as when I-No is hitting her opponents, directly smashing her guitar against the ground, etc.

As of Guilty Gear -Strive-, It is currently in the possession of Axl Low who took Marlene away from I-No during the final battle in her ascent to godhood.

entries.name: May's anchor
entries.content:
May's anchor is an unnamed recurring weapon in the Guilty Gear series. Although anchors are traditionally heavy pieces of metal that allow sailors to hold ships in place, May uses this one as her signature weapon.

Despite the anchor's massive size and weight, she can easily carry it one handed, over her shoulder. Thanks to her incredible strength, she is able to swings it around as if it weighs almost nothing.

entries.name: Ms. Charlotte
entries.content:
Ms. Charlotte is one of Elphelt Valentine's weapon in the Guilty Gear world, introduced in Guilty Gear -Strive- to replace both Ms. Travailler & Ms. Confille in the Xrd series. It is her main weapon. 

It is a magical scroll (marriage certificate) that can take the form of an advanced rifle shaped like a lance, that has a microphone and bow ontop of the lower half on the gun.

The weapon can form various forms of magical projectiles. From short-range blasts to homing orbs. It can also be used for propulsion.

The bow is green, and the gun is white with pink accents.

It can seemingly shapeshift into something similar to Ms. Travailler (A futuristic shotgun).

entries.name: Ms. Confille
entries.content:
Ms. Confille is a recurring weapon in the Guilty Gear series. It is one of the many firearms in Elphelt Valentine's arsenal, just like Ms. Travailler. It is a rifle that was created by the Cyprus Project. 

In 2186, following the Baptisma 13 event, under orders of St. Maximus Ariels and the Conclave, massive resources were dedicated to developing effective countermeasures and weapons against Backyard threats, such as Valentines and Servants. One such as the Cyprus Project, which attempted to understand and advance technology that was lost after the Dawn of Revival under the direction of Leon Mining. Among the weapons the project produced were Ms. Confille, Ms. Travailler, and an unnamed handgun.

Around September 2187, Elphelt Valentine stole a number of firearms—including Ms. Confille—from the research facility on Cyprus, making them her signature weapons.

The gun is shaped like a white punk-rock rifle.

When the trigger is pressed, it forms magical energy into a projectile and fires it, allowing those who lack magical aptitude to still benefit from the use of magical bullets. Ms. Confille was also designed for mid-to long-range combat. It is said to have been developed as an effective countermeasure for Backyard-native threats, who are known for optimizing their magic beyond the Divine Steps, which normally renders common spells useless.

entries.name: Ms. Travailler
entries.content:
Ms. Travailler is a recurring weapon in the Guilty Gear series. It is a shotgun that was created by the Cyprus Project. It is one of the many firearms in Elphelt Valentine's arsenal, just like Ms. Confille.

It looks like an futuristic, rectangular shotgun with a square 4-leaf clover symbol in its' center.

entries.name: Outrage
entries.content:
The Outrage is an extremely powerful amplification device meant to channel and magnify magic energy designed as an anti-Gear weapon by Sol Badguy. The other version of it in the Guilty Gear Xrd games is the Junkyard Dog, which he designed as a "simple" version of the Outrage, although weaker than the original latter due to only having two Sacred Treasures, being designed in its incomplete construction. Until Strive, the Junkyard Dog was modified or returned once again into its (somewhat) complete version, renamed once more as Outrage MK. II.

The original Outrage was created by Sol in retaliation against the restart of the Gear Project and completed by 2074. Because the sheer volume of magical energy produced by its completed form was not easily controlled, the Outrage was split by Sol into eight different components, later called the Sacred Treasures.

The Fireseal & the Thunderseal were later acquired by the Sacred Order of Holy Knights. The Fireseal was later stolen by Sol Badguy & the Thunderseal was given by Kliff Undersn to Ky Kiske.

The Zessen was used to power a Dimensional Barrier that surrounds a Japanese Colony, but was later stolen by Anji Mito (Anji claims he just found it during his travels).

The Flashing Fang was acquired by the Conclave, but stolen from one of their bases named Harden Fort by Sol during the events of Guilty Gear Vastedge XT.

The Outrage is a superweapon intended to be used in concert with the Saint Oratorio, allowing for the transportation of this high-energy spell. It was designed to amplify magic and optimize spell casting—which would improve the wielder's effectiveness in combat—, as well as reduce the chance of magic misfiring. As Frederick developed the Outrage, however, he realized that the power it contained was too much for any human to wield, and not even himself could handle it, so he split it into 8 different parts.

The original Outrage has 2 forms, a "practical form" in the form that appears to be a wand, while it's other form the "temporary assembled form" takes the form of a large mechanical weapon of sorts.

Even after being split into 8, each part is still a source of tremendous power, with normal humans being unable to tap into it. Only those with a strong affinity for magic can truly harness the treasures' power.

entries.name: Ramlethal's greatswords
entries.content:
Ramlethal Valentine's greatswords are a pair of giant swords.

Styled after straight katanas, each of the swords has a long handle and large blade with a angled transition between the edge section of the blade and the point. They are largely differentiated from one another by their red and green colouration. The weapons are usually carried by Lucifero.

entries.name: Raven's needles
entries.content:
Raven's needles are unnamed recurring weapons in the Guilty Gear series.

These four rings that have long needles affixed to them. Wearing them on the index and middle fingers of both hands, Raven uses them as if they were claws.

entries.name: Sin's flag
entries.content:
Sin Kiske's flag is an unnamed recurring weapon in the Guilty Gear world. Being his signature weapon, Sin wields it after heeding Sol's ironic statement "go wave a flag or something" after demanding him for a cool weapon.

He wields it like a staff, having the flag bundled up and kept in place whilst in combat.

entries.name: Testament's scythe
entries.content:
An unnamed scythe is Testament's weapon of choice. A recurring item in the Guilty Gear world, Testament uses it in battle alongside their succubi & EXE Beast.

The scythe blade is made of Testament's blood, extending from a demonic skull is the blood blade that has black symbols on it. the skull that has a spine that wraps around the wooden hilt of the scythe. Testament walks around with the scythes hilt, with a cage on top of it hanging from the skulls mouth, with their Succubi famliars are inside it. In Testaments' intro the cage disappears & the pink succubus is eaten by the gray skull, turning into a pool of blood that forms into the blade, while the cyan succubus turns into a crow.

entries.name: Thunderseal
entries.content:
Thunderseal is Ky Kiske's signature weapon, designed to amplify lightning magic and one of the eight Sacred Treasures that originally formed The Outrage.

When Ky Kiske rose in rank to the leader of the Sacred Order of Holy Knights, the Thunderseal was given to him by Kliff as a recognition to his rise to leadership and skill in lightning magic.

In Lightning the Argent, Sol Badguy confiscated the Thunderseal from Ky to stop him from interfering with his activities. He returned it before Ky faced Sebass.

In Guilty Gear 2 Overture, Ky Kiske used the Thunderseal to stop time itself on the Maiden of the Grove to halt her sublimation, rendering it incorporeal. Ky Kiske used another sword called Aquila during this time. He later acquires a modified sword called Magnolia Éclair in Guilty Gear Vastedge XT.

In Dizzy's arcade mode in Guilty Gear Xrd Rev2 it is shown that the Thunderseal can automatically regenerate after being disassembled, forming into a more traditional sword like shape.

During the events of Guilty Gear -Strive-, Ky  wields the Thunderseal once again, which has taken on a new appearance similar to it's regenerated shape in Guilty Gear Xrd Rev2.

Thunderseal appears as a thin bladed sword, almost akin to a bulky rapier, with a blue-grip and a blue coloured core in the center of the cross-shaped handguard.

entries.name: Venom's pool cue
entries.content:
Venom's signature weapon is a pool cue.

The pool cue is blue at the tip up to the ferrule and the wrap, a silver butt sleeve and a black bumper in the shape of a skull with red eyes - the rest of the cue is white.

When not in use, Venom carries it in a white case with his signature blue eye design on the sides, kept shut by 10 silver toggles with green padding to hold both halves of the cue in place, along with his chalks.

entries.name: Zessen
entries.content: Zessen is Anji Mito's signature weapon and one of the Sacred Treasures that originally formed the Outrage. It was created by the scientist Frederick Bulsara to destroy the Gears. Anji uses the fans to channel and amplify his wind magic. Originally, it was not used as a weapon, but to create and maintain a Dimensional Barrier that surrounded a Japanese Colony.

entries.name: Cradle
entries.content: The Cradle is a vessel controlled by the Conclave, which carries them and the body of Justice. It is capable of moving into the Backyard for limited periods of time and is protected by Absolute Defense: Felion. It also possesses limited artillery capacity though it isn't equipped for combat. But the teleportation process causes some of the Backyard to momentarily bleed into reality, killing every normal living being within the field’s range.

entries.name: May Ship
entries.content:
The May Ship is a recurring airship in the Guilty Gear series. it is carrier-class hover ship captained by Johnny and crewed by the Jellyfish Pirates, and has appeared as battle stage for both Johnny and May. It is succeeded by the May Ship II in the Xrd games.

The May Ship is nearly 250 metres long, 50 metres high, and 30 metres wide (not including wingspan). It has 112 cabins, only a fraction of which are lived-in by the current crew. It contains a large Galley and Mess, full bathroom and shower facilities, various weapon and equipment stores, as well as large compartments for cargo and vehicles. Over the years it has gone through various make-overs (most notably the color and grafitti), but can still be identified as being of Zepp-design in origin.

The May Ship uses large turbine-propulsion systems on the wings and underside to hover and fly. These are powered by a small thermonuclear generator at the heart of the ship, and allow it to reach speeds averaging nearly 180 kilometres per hour. If it were ever destroyed, the resultant detonation would be catastrophic.

In the original Guilty Gear stage, Battles take place in the Ship's wing, where a crew member can be seen waving by a window. Smaller blue and green whale ships can be seem flying behid.

Guilty Gear X features a new Mayship stage; with exposed mechanical parts, and a glass ceilling showing the interior of the ship. Graffitti reading 'L♡VE JOHNNY' and 'MAY SHIP' can be found. In XX, the stage is now set at night, and in Accent Core, it is docked at the sea, seemingly under repairs. Crew members in this itteration don't seem to follow any set design, and are mostly generic bikini and pirate girls.

entries.name: May Ship II
entries.content:
The May Ship II is a recurring airship in the Guilty Gear world, serving as the current home base of the Jellyfish Pirates. It serves as May's battle stage since the Xrd games, having replaced the original May Ship.

The May Ship II is packed with cutting-edge technology, and has a cruising speed of 648 knots. At full engine power, it can reach speeds of up to 3564 knots, making it one of the fastest vessels to roam the skies. It looks like a blue whale.

entries.name: Art of Resurrection
entries.content:
The art of resurrection is a form of magic created by the Conclave.

Originally, it would have been discovered by Dr. Baldhead as part of his medical research. However, the Conclave wanted to keep it a scret for their owns, and to prevent it him from finding the secret they hired the Assassin's Guild. Zato-ONE staged the death of one of Baldhead's patients, causing him to believe that it was a result of his own malpractice and driving him insane.

This technique was later used by the Conclave to bring the aforementioned Zato-ONE back to life in Guilty Gear Xrd -Sign- after his death at the hands of Eddie in Guilty Gear X.

entries.name: Arcanum
entries.content:
The Arcanum is a book that contains 666 known spells discovered in the world of the Guilty Gear world. Six spells have been banned from the Arcanum, deemed too dangerous to be performed.

Little is known about the Arcanum, only that it contains information about 666 spells, yet six of them have been banned, so in actuality there are 660 castable spells. This set of spells are known by the term of Forbidden Magic, and were deemed too dangerous to attempt, or about which too little is known. They involve incredible risk, or can cause horrible side-effects for the caster. These spells are referred to as Forbidden Magic Spells or Covenants of the Condemned or Hell's Fall Techniques, along with a cardinal number. Currently, only two of them are known:

The 5th Forbidden Magic Spell, also known as Life-Eating Shadow or Pact of the Shadows, binds a Forbidden Beast to the caster's shadow, although using the shadow too much will erode the host's life force. The researcher who discovered the spell was so afraid of its effects he put a seal of protection on it that required anyone who cast it to give up their sight. It was used by Zato-ONE, who became a host to Eddie.
The 6th Forbidden Magic Spell, also called Angra, is a spell that, upon casting, enables the user to freely manipulate and control their hair by paying a steep, but unknown price. It was used by Millia Rage, but it is unclear if she took the curse freely or if it was forced upon her.
Otherwise, the current contents of the Arcanum are unknown. It can be assumed, however, that many of the playable cast's abilities are based upon the spells written here. Known spells or types of magic that could be written here include:

Element generation - Simply manifesting one of the elements to appear, e.g. cause fire, or light up a small area. Likely, Sol's Gun-Flame and Ky's Stun Edge are examples of this.
Seal - It is a form of magic that allows the user to imprison objects, or more commonly, people. The Barrier Prison, and its stronger form the Dimensional Prison, are magicks of this type.
Bind - This type of magic immobilizes a target in a given spot. Anji is able to use them.
Barrier - Magic of this type enables the caster to produce a shield around something for whatever purpose, generally used as a protective measure. The most powerful known spell of this type is Absolute Defense: Felion, which can only be cast by the Conclave or the Sanctus Populi.
Float - A spell that enables the caster to float in midair; it is not a difficult ability, but maintaining a state of floating through inertia and friction requires a lot of training and time to execute. That Man is capable of casting it.
Summoning - The act of calling forth objects or even living beings is possible, as demonstrated by May, Testament, Faust, and Baiken.
Spatial Deformation - One of the most powerful types of magic, which can only used by those who fully grasp the theoretical underpinnings of magic and have a gift for information manipulation. Faust's abilities are believed to be of this type. Raven also seems to have a certain mastery over Spatial Deformation magic, beating Faust.
Teleportation - ...
Telecommunication - ...
Climate control - ...

entries.name: Arcanum History
entries.content:
Upon discovering the existence of the Backyard in the late 20th century, The Original laid the foundation for what would become the study of magic. When he realized his error in creating the Universal Will, he warned the scientific community of an incoming catastrophe, but only a few—those who came to be known as the Apostles—listened. When his prediction came to pass in form of the Dawn of Revival, only his disciples were prepared to provide swift relief to mankind.

In order to restore human civilization, they they helped the world adapt to magic. Though the early stages of magic research were difficult, the Apostles continued to push forward, expanding human knowledge of magic very quickly. The results of that process were, presumably, published in the form of the Arcanum, but the original research that led to the book's creation remains in possession of the Apostles, nowadays known as the Conclave.

entries.name: Absolute World
entries.content:
Absolute World, also called World of Absolution, is a term that refers to a momentary state in which the boundaries between the present world and the Backyard are blurred, as if they merged for a second.

An Absolute World occurs when two forms of informational bodies—"Adam" and "Eve" for ease of reference—appear simultaneously within the Backyard. In general, both appear for a split second, and then disappear immediately, in alternating intervals. In the event that they both appear, the boundaries between the present world and the Backyard are blurred or merged, and anything that cannot withstand that state of dense informational pressure is erased. As such, it is a mass extinction event that affects the entire universe.

"Adam", or the Flame of Corruption, and "Eve", the Scales of Juno, have neither a will nor intelligence, and can survive extinction as they are arguably immortal.

According to Bedman, since the Backyard is connected to peoples' dreams, dream and reality are superimposed on each other during an Absolute World. As within his own dreams Bedman can cause certain phenomena to occur—of which only death is permanent—, he believes that he can change reality (including saving his sister and undoing all the deaths he caused) during this momentary event.

entries.name: Absolute World History
entries.content:
In the Backyard, a space superordinate to the universe wherein Earth exists, there are two forms of informational bodies that have neither a will nor intelligence. Arguably immortal, they are believed to have existed for billions of years.

After life first appeared on Earth four billion years ago, there have been five large-scale extinction events since the appearance of multicellular organisms. Over the course of history, five Absolute Worlds appear to have occurred resulting in the Big Five, five mass extinctions experienced by creatures on Earth during the Ordovician, Devonian, Permian, Triassic, and Cretaceous Periods.

Sometime in the 20th century, The Original entered the Backyard and discovered the existence of these two informational bodies, and named them "Flame of Corruption" and "Scales of Juno". Then, to ensure that an Absolute World never occurs again, he sealed them into two separate "seeds" or cores. Sometime between 2010 and 2014, The Original returned to the Backyard to stop his own creation, and entrusted his fifth disciple, That Man, with the seeds.

In 2016, upon learning that his friend Aria Hale was terminally ill, That Man begged Aria to let herself be cryo-frozen until a cure was found. However, she stubbornly refused, wanting to spend her last moments with Frederick Bulsara, rather than face a future without them. In his desperation, That Man implanted the Flame of Corruption within Frederick (without his consent) to make him "indestructable", turning him into a Gear, and Aria finally agreed to cryosleep. In 2073, That Man transformed Aria into the basis of what would become Justice and appears to have implanted Scales of Juno within the Gear commander. That Man later created a failsafe version of this core and planted it inside of Jack-O' Valentine, though these two versions became one when Jack-O' and Justice merged in 2187 to restore Aria Hale.

It is implied that both Sol and Jack-O' are "half complete", and that the informational bodies within the seeds have yet to be "restored". As some have noted, their death would release the cores and potentially cause an Absolute World to occur.

entries.name: Absolute Defense: Felion
entries.content: Absolute Defense: Felion is an ultimate defensive spell that fully negates physical and magical assaults. It can also be utilized as a Barrier Prison to contain powerful mages such as That Man. Originally, only the members of the Conclave and the Sanctus Populi Maximus, Ariels, were capable of executing this spell. However, both Bedman and Ky Kiske have demonstrated that they can cast the spell as well.

entries.name: Backyard
entries.content:
The Backyard is an alternate world in Guilty Gear. It is said to contain all the information that creates the real world. It is also an encapsulating term that refers to the source of limitless energy known as Magic. It is the codex or source of transferred information that comprises most of the world as physical manifested data; the source of what makes the real world exist. The world itself is said to be a virtual space, resulted from the information conveyed from the Backyard. Upon entry to the Backyard, the extremely restricted data pressure is immense and anyone who enters must be "tuned" to the frequency the Backyard emits in order not to be crushed by the dense information contained within it. That Man is known to have kept and constructed the "Cube" within this location.

The existence of the Backyard is first revealed in Guilty Gear 2 -Overture-, when Sol Badguy visited Dr. Paradigm in Ganymede. Youkai like Izuna and the Valentines originate from the dimension.

The Backyard is described as being "similar to the relationship between a game and the computer", and said to be like a book containing the theory of the world, essentially being the equivalent of the Akashic Records within the Guilty Gear Universe. The mechanical process of producing a reality is created by various factors. Anything that happens in the real world cannot affect the Backyard; however, certain elements within the Backyard can apply and change this world's existence. Various places, like the Underworld (Guilty Gear Judgment), act as parts and "layers" of the Backyard, and by definition, those beings that live within the various levels connected to the Backyard or within the Backyard itself that are not artificially constructed are called "Youkai". Demons, monsters, mushi, mutants, ghosts, Guardian Spirits, and deities are implied to be those creatures. The Original Man was the first human to have ever entered the Backyard and come back alive. Following this, he comprised all of his knowledge of the Backyard into a book known as the Sage's Testament.

Normal humans are unable to survive within the Backyard as they are instantly crushed to dust within moments, with special cases able to survive up to about 32 hours before needing to return to the physical world.

entries.name: Black Technology
entries.content:
Black Techology is the term that refers to a set of technology and science that is forbidden in Guilty Gear.

In the 21st century, the urgency to preserve the environment became critical, and forced scientists to discover alternate methods of advancement. With the occurrence of the Dawn of Revival banning all electronic technologies and the discovery of magic in 2010, mainstream science began to be taken over by magical science. Eventually, mainstream technology was banned by the UN and the term "Black Tech" was coined. The IPF became in charge in regulating technology and people who are selling, using or owning Black Tech is penalized. It's also illegal to spread knowledge about Black Tech. The only exception to this policy is the nation of Zepp.

The entirety of the technological ban eventually result in the creation of magi-tech to replace conventional technology, which vehicles are now powered by magic or firearms now used magical elements as ammunitions. The best example is the US infantry is shown to carry magic rifles or the US president uses a magic-powered limo for transportation. In the Guilty Gear X Drama CD, a drunk Axl who mentioned E=MC^2 was almost arrested by the police.

entries.name: Bounty
entries.content:
A bounty is a monetary reward offered for Gears or criminals that the authorities want captured or removed. They are a recurring element in the Guilty Gear world.

Among these monetary rewards, Gear bounties are usually quite high. Anyone who collects a bounty is technically a bounty hunter, but usually the term is used to describe those who make a living from collecting bounties. Sol Badguy is one such person. When someone captures or otherwise fulfills a bounty, it is their responsibility to deliver the bounty, or proof of some kind, to the Post-War Administration Bureau.

entries.name: Cube
entries.content: The Cube is a structure built by That Man which is located within the Backyard. The 'Key' to unlocking the Cube are the Prime Gear cells of Justice. The Cube is said to have the power to manipulate the information of the Backyard, allowing it to influence the real world on a universal scale. The Magic Chord Signature of the Cube is stated to be exactly like the Chord Signature of Sol's Gear body, but the significance of this is unknown. During the Baptisma 13 incident, Valentine attempted to obtain the Key to access the Cube, however she was ultimately thwarted by Sol Badguy who returned the Cube to its original form and shattered the door to prevent anyone from entering it.

entries.name: Gold Series
entries.content: The Gold Series are soldiers who can block out pain, enhance their aggression and magic, and temporarily take on Gear-like characteristics. In structure, they are similar to Eddie and Millia Rage's hair, however, they were created through the use of Zepp technology.

entries.name: Gear Cell Suppressor
entries.content: The Gear Cell Suppressor is the red metal headband that Sol Badguy wears on his forehead. It is designed to both isolate and regulate the Gear cells in his body in order for him maintain a humanoid appearance, as well as conceals the crimson Gear Mark on his forehead. It also acts a limiter that keeps the majority of Sol's Magic Energy suppressed.

entries.name: G4 Summit
entries.content: The Group of Four, abbreviated as G4, is an international in-house meeting between the heads of the four developed countries. This four countries involved are the United Kingdoms of Illyria, United States of America, Chinese Federation, and Southern Hemisphere Oceania Federation. The heads of each country are allowed to be able to bring in a single knight to guard them during their visit in the meeting.

entries.name: Imitation Series
entries.content:
The Imitation Series is a robotics project by the Post-War Administration Bureau that focuses on creating mechanical replicas of notable fighters via data collection. The most famous of these robots is Robo-Ky.

Created by Crow Kuruwaba, the Imitation Series are meant to achieve the same capabilities and appearance as the subject they imitate, and meant to be mass-produced. There are currently only two such series.

The Robo-Ky series, bases on legendary child prodigy Ky Kiske, were considered obsolete due to their mediocre combat statistics and glitches in their A.I. that made too independent as well as insubordinate. The other were the "Justice" clones. The combat data upon which they rely is from Second Holy Order Selection Tournament.

entries.name: Magic
entries.content: Magic, also called sorcery, is a limitless form of natural energy in the Guilty Gear world. First introduced in the original Guilty Gear, it is the source of the combatants' manifested powers and the abnormalities that occur in the world. While its discovery solved the energy crisis that humanity faced in the 21st century, it is also a primary cause of turmoil in the world.

entries.name: Magic History
entries.content:
Magic has always existed, as it is simply the materialization of the pure natural energy of the Backyard into the world, and awareness of ki—one of magic's five context—by Eastern cultures likely dates as far back as 500 BC.

It wasn't until sometime in the late 20th century that knowledge of the phenomenon was formalized. The man known as The Original discovered the Backyard's existence and laid the foundation for what would become the study of magic, the Theory of Magical Science. However, he made the mistake of creating the Universal Will. Realizing the entity's dark intentions, The Original suddenly began to tell anyone who would listen that the world had to abandon its reliance on electronics or face dire consequences, but he was met with disappointment and then embarrassment by the scientific community that once respected him.

Only a few listened to him, and four of his five disciples made preparations for a technology-free world. Then in the year 1999, the Dawn of Revival occurred, and the Universal Will attempted to manifest itself through electronic circuitry. The UN banned all such devices, but with the technology that had supported society now gone, the world quickly devolved into chaos. Less than a year later, the Original and disciples set to work restoring human civilization, becoming "the saviors of humankind".

Earning thousands of followers with their efficient relief, they helped the world adapt to magic. In the early stages of magic research, mages had difficulty controlling feedback from the Backyard, which resulted in frequent misfires and explosions, with more than a few people dead or injured as a result. Nevertheless, the Apostles continued to push forward, expanding human knowledge of magic very quickly, and bringing about the Age of Magic.

As the Apostles' magical expertise grew, so did their influence. In 2008, they formed the Sanctus Populi, and their discipless began to travel the world, spreading their teachings. In 2010, the United Nations declared sorcery and magic the new standard, and science and industry, sources of environmental pollution and weapons of mass destruction, were outlawed. Only a few organizations, like Zepp, attempted to keep the old sciences and cultures alive. Around this time, the Apostles reformed into the Conclave, and The Original parted this world to stop the Universal Will's rampage, leaving the "seeds" of the Absolute World to That Man, his fifth disciple.

The introduction of magic shifted the world's production balance greatly, and while technologically it took several steps back, more value was placed on cultural advancements. Nonetheless, political and economic power became synonymous with zeal and instroments, and given that the UN and Vatican oversaw the process, a large gap appeared between Europe and the Americas by 2042. A figurative war thus erupted, fueled by rapidly developing magical theory, that saw the birth of Gears—powerful biological weapons produced by fusing human and animal DNA with magic—, and led to the century-long Crusades, which began in 2074 and concluded in 2175 with the Sealing of Justice.

Although magic currently exists almost everywhere in common life, very few people know how it actually functions. After the end of the war, with the world going into restoration mode, the UN's standardized curriculum was thus revised to include the subject of Basic Magical Theory. Physics is also heavily linked with magic, appearing as "Magic Physics".

entries.name: Magic Usage
entries.content:
The practical application of magic theory is called a spell, of which there are 666 known ones. A spell is derived from formulas that draw energy from another plane—the Backyard—and convert it into more useful and familiar forms, which some consider similar to alchemy. In mainstream magic, the tuning, i.e. inscription or transmission of magical energy, requires a language hierarchy known as the Divine Steps, twelve perceivable words that are, apparently, arranged into a chord. There are several "local" rules that must also be respected in order to cast a spell.

The effect and strength of magic is determined by how many words are lined up, recited simultaneously, and how they are arranged. The practitioner must memorize their order and recite them accordingly; these twelve words are complicated, but there are infinite possibilities of wordings. Spells that produce nearly identical results can be inscribed in significantly different ways. If a spell works on a deeper level than what the caster is able to interpret, they will be unable to cast it. It is possible to optimize magic beyond the Divine Steps, as demonstrated by the Vizuel, Dr. Paradigm, and Izuna, which renders common spells useless unless given a unique blessing.

entries.name: Magic Development
entries.content:
Creating magic is a highly involved process: the writer, sometimes called programmer, who must have a state-mandated license to hold such a position, writes the necessary programmatic language to cause magic to occur, and logs it in a score in the appropriate format. Sometimes a score is called a note or program. Primary recording mediums include zeal or paper, and based on what the score says (e.g. "cause fire" or "fly"), the person activating the spell is able to cause a desired effect.

Finally, a sequencer is a catalyst required to play the score. Depending on the sequencer type or score, the final effect will vary greatly. The sequencer can be:

A hardware sequencer, also called an instroment, which is a physical device that will load a score and play it back, but cannot alter the score's contents. "Pods" are a combination of a score and sequencer used in common households; they are designed for a specific purpose—e.g. lighting or as an engine—, and cannot perform complex tasks. A physical sequencer of better quality, like the Sacred Treasures, can have a wider range of applications, and even enable to adjust output as desired.

A software sequencer, which is the act of tapping directly into the Backyard to cause spells that produce similar or desired effects. Altering the score's contents is possible this way, but rigorous training is required to reach this skill level.

The reason for using a physical sequencer is the issue in processing speed, but also makes spells much safer and stable. With a software sequencer there is no guarantee that the desired effect will occur every time, and the casting process is very long and tedious. Still, practitioners of this caliber can find professional work as "engineers", editing scores and arrange the perfect desired output for a given scenario or situation. "Sorcerers", for their part, can wield magic without any external catalysts with short casting times, although they focus more in R&D. Both are hired by the government or massive corporations, but obtaining a license is extremely dreary.

entries.name: Magic Type
entries.content:
Magic works according to the so-called five element configuration. There are five basic types of magical energy: Fire, Lightning, Water, Wind, and Ki. Every form of magic is inevitably made up of at least one of these attributes. Generally, magic users adhere to a singular element, and it is rare for someone to command more than one. It is unknown how some high-level magic—e.g. Faust's displacement and spatial abilities, I-No and Axl's time travel, May and Testament's summons, or the Soul Sinker—fits into this categorization system, or even if they are part of it at all.

Fire : The destructive power of Fire magic appears to be rather common, as many characters show the power the use flames during their attacks, perhaps being the easiest to use. The Fireseal is able to concentrate and amplify Fire magic used by its wielder. Character who use the Fire element are: Sol Badguy, Axl Low, and presumably, Dizzy, Jam Kuradoberi and Justice.

Lightning / Thunder: Said to be the most difficult attribute to master, Lightning yields destructive potency that rivals Fire-type spells. The Thunderseal is able to concentrate and amplify Lightning magic used by its wielder. Character who use the Lightning element are: Ky Kiske, Robo-Ky, Sin Kiske, and presumably, Justice and Dizzy.

Water: No users of this element are known, however, May's summons—hinted by the present water effects—could imply that she uses Water-type magic, in addition to Ki. Dizzy's spells, via Undine, also seem to be Water-elemental in nature.

Wind: Very little information has been given about Wind-type magic. The Zessen concentrates and amplify Wind magic used by its wielder. The only known user is Anji Mito, owner of the aforementioned weapon. Johnny's Mist Finer and I-No's attacks could possibly involve Wind magic as well.

Ki (otherwise known as qi (chi): The least understood of all elemental components, unique in that it can oppose or amplify the other four elements. Researchers and theorists have worked hard to understand the inner workings of ki, but thus far they have met with little success. Unlike the other elements, every person has some ki, even without specific training, as it is a part of nature and exists within every living thing. It often responds to powerful emotions. There have been recorded cases of children manipulating ki but losing the ability to do so as they grow older, likely due to a greater emotional stability. It is a rare ability, however: not many people can see the flow of ki, let alone wield it. Users include Chipp Zanuff, Tsuyoshi, Kliff Undersn, Mizuha, Jam Kuradoberi, Kum Haehyun, and presumably, May, Baiken, and Anji Mito.
Ki is heavily linked to the spirituality of Eastern cultures, who were the most adept at harnessing it. Some conspiracy theorists believe that this is exactly why they were obliterated by Justice, though for certain only the Kum family was cornered into extinction by the Gear commander because of it. Throughout the world, the Post-War Administration Bureau expresses interest in obtaining and further studying the power, having to do so by capturing those of Japanese descent, as they are all able to manipulate ki. Unique to them is the Ki Overflow Syndrome.

An additional element has been mentioned—Light, which is known to manifest via the Flashing Fang, but it is unknown if it is simply made up of the aforementioned elements, or if it is a separate one altogether.

entries.name: Opus
entries.content:
The Opus are man-made anti-Valentine units which were constructed following the Baptisma 13 incident in order to counter future Valentine attacks. Development of the Opus was instructed by the Sanctus Populi and championed by its leader Maximus Ariels, with the United Kingdom of Illyria leading development.

When the Cradle appears near the Black Sea on October 29, 2187, the Opus units that are present survive the sphere that expands from the Cradle before it disappears (actually an intrusion of space from the Backyard). Research by Dr. Paradigm reveals the Opus are in fact Gears, a fact which shocks Leo Whitefang and President Vernon when Paradigm reveals it to them. During the final phases of the Conclave's plan, they use Justice's ability to command Gears to turn the Opus against the defenders of Illyria Castle.

entries.name: St. Elmo's Fire
entries.content:
St. Elmo's Fire or St. Elmo is a huge and mysterious bolt of lightning which strikes once every 13 years. There is no meteorological explanation for the lightning bolt, but it usually occurs some time around late October and early November.

During the Crusades, the occurrence of St. Elmo saved humanity when it was cornered by the Gears. The lightning fell on the Gear army, wiping out a large portion of their forces. Since then, humanity has celebrated the arrival of St. Elmo's Fire. During its destructive power, easily capable of wiping out an entire city, Illyria Castle was constructed as a lightning rod to attract it and protect the surrounding areas.

During Guilty Gear Xrd -Sign-, the Conclave intends to use the energy from St. Elmo harnessed via Illyria Castle to activate Justice, however Dr. Paradigm with help from Dizzy amplifies the energy from the lightning strike and overloads the system.

entries.name: Soul Sinker
entries.content:
Soul Sinker is a phenomenon related to Masterghosts, into physical reality in order to create powerful familiars known as Servants.

The risks involved in manifesting a Master Ghost is the obliteration of one's soul should it be destroyed.

entries.name: Saint Oratorio
entries.content:
Saint Oratorio is a destructive and incredibly dangerous spell that consists of an intense bursts of raw magic that can annihilate anything in its path. It is specifically meant to be used in concert with the Outrage.

The spell was being developed prior to 2014 by the "Saint Oratorio Project".

Sol Badguy designed the Junkyard Dog with a secondary function to transfigure into a long-range cannon that can fire a weak version of Saint Oratorio. However, the backlash from unleashing this spell is tremendous, causing it to not only cause significant damage to the target and environment, but the user as well, which is why Sol uses it sparingly.

entries.name: Tome of Origin
entries.content:
The Tome of Origin is a book that The Original sealed the essence of the Backyard into, far back in the past of the Guilty Gear world.

Sometime in 20th century, a man now only known as The Original—who would go on to lay the foundation for what would become the study of magic—discovered the existence of the Backyard. Somehow he managed to enter this realm and return, though he realized that "No evil should touch this place." The Original then sealed all that the Backyard was into a single tome, hoping that mankind would never stumble upon its power.

It is revealed in Strive that Asuka actually fused the Tome of Origin within his body in order to prevent from being given in its wrong hands. This leads Asuka to handcraft a fake version of this Tome to fool Happy Chaos

entries.name: Tuning
entries.content:
Tuning is a unique form of energy manipulation. Due to tuning existing before the introduction of magic, it could be considered either similar to or an application of ki manipulation. Tuners, as described by Johnny, are able to "tune" people like one tunes a guitar, helping safeguard them from illness and realize their true potential. The only surviving tuners are those of the Kum family, especially family head Kum Haehyun.

Tuning has multiple uses, both offensively and defensively. Haehyun states that while she can't use it to cure illness, she is able to strength the bodies of others to help prevent them from falling ill in the first place. During Ariels' attempt to transform the residents of the Japanese colony into antimatter Gears using their Ki Overflow Syndrome, Haehyn uses her tuning with the help of a ki-infused cherry blossom to block her attempts. Haehyun also uses it to bolster the strength of her attacks, create "tuning balls" as projectiles, and paralyze her opponents.

entries.name: Universal Will
entries.content:
The Universal Will, also translated as the Merciless Apocalypse, is a mysterious entity originating from the Backyard. It's directly responsible for the Dawn of Revival and the creation and actions of the Valentines (who refer to it as their "Mother",) and indirectly responsible for the Crusades, the actions of the Conclave and the Post-War Administration Bureau after the Crusades, as well as the actions of Asuka R. Kreutz in opposition to it, making it the ultimate evil of the Guilty Gear universe. Its current human avatar is the former Sanctus Maximus Populi Ariels.

The Universal Will is a "like a robot" and is bound by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics. In order to bypass the first law during its conflict with the Original, it took the desires extracted from I-No and implanted them in the Original. This drove him insane and made him lose his humanity.

In preparing to fight Sol, the Universal Will realized that it needed to understand humans, and remembering that the Original was once human, merged with him, then went on to possess Ariels (and probably Hapinus before that). The overwhelming desires of humankind are what ultimately drove Ariels insane, just like the Original. And after his spirit escaped Ariels's body following her defeat, he took on the name Happy Chaos.

entries.name: Universal Will History
entries.content:
Some time in the late 20th century, the man who would become known as The Original discovered and accessed the Backyard. During his studies, he created an information organism whose directive to ensure eternal happiness for humans without harming them. But the Original made a critical error in not defining humans, with his creation pondering over it before reaching the conclusion that humans possess a "soul" and thus must have free will and choice. But it then realizes that humanity is gradually discarding their free will due to the natural state of human advancement and bringing humans eternal happiness would only help the process along. This conundrum allowed the entity to conclude that real humans don't yet exist, circumventing it’s programming by seeing the current "human” race as "redundancies" that must be exterminated to make way for true humans of its own making. The entity would later be christened as the Universal Will.

In 1999, the Universal Will made its first move in manifesting in electronic devices worldwide to broadcast a message: "In a matter of days, humanity will crumble." Several days later, all electronic devices ceased functioning and multiple natural disasters bombarded civilization in an event known as the Dawn of Revival, leading to worldwide societal collapse until The Original and his disciples introduced magic to the world. At some point after this, The Original disappeared, re-entering the Backyard in an attempt to stop the Universal Will once and for all. His fate is currently unknown.

The Universal Will launched a second attack in the year 2074, simultaneously attempting to manifest inside and seize control of a newly-activated Justice, as well as manifesting in the people of Japan, triggering a reaction that transformed them into antimatter Gears. Seeing the coming end of the world right before his eyes, Asuka R. Kreutz seized control of Justice himself and fired her Gamma Ray at Japan, reducing the island nation to a deep crater in the ocean. Both the contact with the Universal Will and her actions psychologically scarred Justice and drove her berserk as she took control of all Gears and declaring war on humanity, marking the beginning of the Crusades.

At some point between 2175 and 2187, the Universal Will approached Bedman in the Backyard and manipulates him into helping it create an "Absolute World" with the lie that he can use his powers to pull his sister Delilah from the Backyard and cure their condition while keeping him in the dark of the event’s purpose in destroying all life on Earth. The Universal Will also began its third attempt to manifest in the real world by possessing a human body to understand human emotions.

The Sanctus Maximus Populi Hapinus the 27th was driven insane and eventually met an early end in 2177, and Ariels took the position as the new avatar of the Universal Will. Developing a hatred for redundancies with her newfound emotions, Ariels began to manipulate events more directly. During this time, she herded the surviving Japanese together into various colonies, ostensibly for their own protection. In 2185, the Universal Will created the first Valentine, an entity born in the Backyard with a single-minded drive to carry out orders implanted in her by "Mother". Valentine invaded the Kingdom of Illyria with an army known as the Vizuel with the goal of obtaining a "key" from the descendants of Justice (either Dizzy or Sin would do,) that would allow her to unlock the Cube, a device in the Backyard that would allow her to take control of the Backyard itself. Valentine was ultimately thwarted and killed by Sol and company, and the events were dubbed the Baptisma 13 incident.

In 2187, two more Valentines were created: Ramlethal and Elphelt. Realizing that the original Valentine's failure came from a lack of emotions, the Universal Will embedded the two with emotions from the outset. Ramlethal allied herself with the Conclave to carry out their secret plan of reviving Justice, while Elphelt was made into a sleeper agent, infiltrating Sol's group with no knowledge of her orders until she was activated. Once again, the Universal Will's plans were thwarted, with Justice's revival ending in failure and the members of the Conclave save Chronus being killed, along with Ramlethal turning against her Mother. However, the Universal Will was able to retrieve Justice's body for another attempt, and Elphelt was activated and retrieved to be used as Justice's new consciousness. To gather the energy necessary for the second revival attempt, she would once again weaponize the Japanese, transforming them into Anti-Matter gears and triggering them to explode en masse. After some test runs, the Universal Will finally revealed her true identity to the public before dropping a small army of antimatter Gears on Illyria City and leaving to attend to Justice's body. However, yet again her plans were thwarted; attempts to transform more Japanese were stopped by Kum Haehyun's Tuning, Illyria was saved by the Assassin's Guild, Zepp and various other characters coming to the rescue, Bedman was defeated by Venom when he was finally forced to awaken to counter his Terra Machina System, and Sol and company discovered Justice's location, retrieving Elphelt from Justice's body and replacing her with Jack-O, an unknown fourth Valentine created by Asuka R. Kreutz to revert Justice back into Aria. The fate of the Universal Will is currently unknown after its defeat, but its human host Ariels is currently under strict detainment by the Illyrian government and her status as Sanctus Maximus has been stricken from history.

entries.name: World Dollar
entries.content: World Dollar is the universal currency used in everywhere in the World.

entries.name: Baptisma 13
keys: invasion of United Kingdom of Illyria
entries.content:
The Baptisma 13 incident is the official name of the invasion of United Kingdom of Illyria by the original Valentine and her Vizuel army in 2186 that takes place during Guilty Gear 2 -Overture-.

Valentine, and to an extent the Universal Will, desired to enter the Cube, a structure built by That Man located in the Backyard that is capable of manipulating information in the Backyard thus influencing the real world.

Unfortunately, they need a "key", the gear cells of Justice, to open it. Thus gears all over Illyria began to disappear and sublimate by Valentine and her army in an effort to find the key. Eventually, Dizzy Justice's daughter was targeted and was close to being sublimated; thankfully High King Ky Kiske managed to use the Thunderseal and froze time around her, saving her from a grim fate.

Unfortunately, with the location of the "key" revealed to them, the Vizuel army launched an all out attack against the capitol of Illyria in order to claim her.

Despite being armed with magic, they were ineffective against the Vizuel army and the city fell, with King Ky being trapped in a seal.

Sometime later, Sol Badguy, Sin Kiske and Izuna arrived and fought their way to the castle, clashing with Valentine in the process. The group managed to reach the throne room but were unable to free Ky from his seal. Sol and Izuna then traveled to Ganymede to get Dr. Paradigm to help while Sin was left behind to watch over Ky.

After passing Paradigm's test and repelling the Vizuel invasion of the archipelago; the doctor along with several of his Gear companions agreed to travel with the Sol back to Illyria. Paradigm was able to release Ky, but Sin was captured and brainwashed by Valentine, which meant she was able to obtain the "key" since Sin was Dizzy's son.

entries.name: Crusades
entries.content: The Crusades is a hundred-year war between Gears and humanity, led by the Sacred Order of Holy Knights, that began with Justice's awakening in 2074 until she was finally sealed away in 2175. When the Crusades at last came to an end, humankind was victorious, but no part of the planet was spared its ramifications.

entries.name: Crusade History
entries.content:
Following the creation of Gears by That Man's Gear Project, the United States of America began to mass produce Gears in 2065—designed to be little more than slaves, incapable of independent thought—and to deploy them to allies across the globe, bringing countless other lands under its control. In 2073, That Man, secretly opposed to their use in war, thus decided to create a Gear that could command it own kind to stop the wars, whom he named Justice. In 2074, an incident occurred, however, which caused Justice to forget her identity and resulted in the destruction of Japan.

Justice thus "awakened" and, announcing herself to be self-aware, took command of all Gears across the globe, gathering an army, and declared war on all mankind. With little documentation of the truth of his research, That Man—his identity unknown due to joining the project under an alias—was widely believed to be the one pulling the strings behind the scenes since he had created Justice. Called "That Man" because no one knew where the blame really lay and his intentions were unclear, That Man was labeled a war criminal who had intentionally turned Justice against humanity.

In wake of heavy initial casualties, humans put their differences aside and formed the Sacred Order of Holy Knights to combat them. Immediately following the disappearance of Japan, America turned into a battlefield and suffered massive damage, such as New York being destroyed. The conflict was then centered around Russia and her neighboring European nations, but the fighting quickly spread, and the war soon engulfed the entire planet. The overwhelming power of the Gears brought humanity to the brink of extinction. Victims from around the world would seek refuge in Australia. For a time there was a period of stability and peace in the region, but eventually Gears gradually began to drive people away until mankind was forced to ultimately abandon the continent. The Tasmanian Islands then became a headquarters of operations that created a perimeter, not letting any Gears enter or exit.

At one point, hundreds of Gears laid siege to Rome, backing humankind into a corner. When things were at their grimmest, a bolt of lightning—to be later named St. Elmo's Fire—struck the Gear horde. It saved several members of the Holy Order, gave them the advantage and ultimately allowed mankind to triumph.

One notable event was the sealing of Hydra, a Megadeath-class Gear that attacked and destroyed London in under an hour. The Order's forces were unable to defeat it, and it rampaged for a day and a night, until Commander Kliff Undersn arrived and fought the beast single-handedly for seven days and nights. He successfully managed to sever three of its five heads and other limbs. Unable to spare more time on finishing off the massive Gear, the Order sealed the Hydra away.

During the Crusades, mankind's desire for a brighter tomorrow was so strong it resulted in the creation of a Magical Foci after their emotions were focused on a single "object", the Backyard. The Backyard interpreted this as an error that would destroy the world. To overcome the crisis, it sealed that conscious away in a single human's body, placing within I-No all the irregularities. She was discovered by The Original, who saw that her godhood was nigh and decided that she was a threat. His solution was to rid her of human desire, taking away her power and her sense of self, but the Universal Will punished him and made him I-No's "other half", formed of mankind's wishes. Also during the war, That Man appeared in many different times, places and disguises, being responsible for the destruction of Baiken's colony; in truth, these appearances were that of the corrupted Original who wreaked havoc by possessing people in his spirit form while calling himself "That Man."

A pivotal event was the Battle of Rome in 2173, in which a horde of about 200 Gears attacked the city. The local army tried to fend off the menace, and sent a distress call. Despite Order headquarters telling to wait for reinforcements and the mission amounting to suicide, battalion captain Ky Kiske responded in hopes of ensuring the safety of its citizens. They resisted until 15 minutes were needed for everyone to be safe; due to soldiers reaching their limit, the Order began its retreat. In one outcome, Ky was killed trying to ensure that I-No—thinking her to be a civilian—was safe, and telling Sol Badguy to become the Order's next commander. Upon seeing the future ramifications (the war lasting until 2181, Dizzy taking over the late Justice as commander, and humanity about to be eradicated) and meeting That Man, I-No went back in time and ensured that Ky lived, later succeeding Kliff as the Order's commander.

In 2175, the war came to an end with the sealing of Justice, with humankind finally victorious through the combined efforts of the Holy Order and Sol Badguy. In one account, Kliff challenged Justice to one last battle; upon Kliff's defeat, Ky stepped in to save the former commander and fought Justice for the first time. Forced to retreat, Justice found herself before Sol, and they fought evenly. During the fight, Justice learned that Sol was a Gear after breaking his headband, but his immunity to being controlled took Justice by surprise and Sol was able to defeat her. Ky, following her trail, found her weakened amidst lava and flames and ordered all support units to engage and seal Justice away in an impenetrable dimensional prison.

In the aftermath, most of the masterless Gear were rounded up and destroyed, and certain Gears—having entered a dormant state—were sealed and safeguarded for their worth as data. Those that gained self-consciousness of their own went into hiding at Ganymede, and most national leaders called for Gear research to be terminated immediately. From 2176 onwards, the day Justice was sealed into her dimensional prison would be used as the date for the Sanctus Populi's Celebration of Victory.

entries.name: Dawn of Revival
entries.content:
The Dawn of Revival is a historical event of great importance that occurred in 1999, in which machines of all types began to malfunction due to an mysterious entity. It led to a worldwide ban on technology and eventually culminated in the Age of Magic.

In 1999, a prophet known only as "the Original" foretold a calamity that would shake the very foundations of human society, finding only a few disciples who heeded his warnings. Although the scientific community was disappointed then embarrassed, the world's superpowers declared a state of emergency.

On an otherwise unremarkable day, every electronic device capable of communicating information—television, radio, the internet—was suddenly invaded. For several hours, the entire planet experienced what appeared to be a form of life. Across every network, on every device, in every language, a single message was broadcast: "In a matter of days, humanity will crumble." Several days later, all electronic devices ceased working, and machines of all types began to malfunction, and humans quickly began to panic. Then, at that moment, several cities around the world were struck by natural disasters—some of them wiped completely off the map.

In the wake of this devastation, humanity had felt the "divine will", and began to believe in some sort of higher order. An investigation showed that the creature had attempted to manifest itself through electronic circuitry. As a result, in an emergency summit, the United Nations banned all electronic devices, effective immediately. Despite requiring an overhaul of nearly every industry, few objected to the changes.

With the technology that had supported it now gone, human society quickly devolved into chaos: food and even water were suddenly in short supply, as transporting them was next to impossible. Human culture thus began to deteriorate and the framework of society, to collapse. However, that same year, the Original and his disciples—who would come to be known, respectively, as "the Savior" and his "Apostles"—had made already preparations for a technology-free world and set to work on restoring human civilization and culture. Their swift and efficient relief earned them immediate support and thousands of new followers, leading to the foundation of the Sanctus Populi in 2008. They taught Magic to the people, thus halting the social collapse, and governments around the world began to research practical applications of this new power source. The Apostles, as "special ambassadors", were dispatched across the globe to spread their knowledge to the masses.

In 2010, the UN declared sorcery and magic the new standard, and called for all nations to dismantle their traditional weapons and technology. Over the next several decades, the UN and the Sanctus Populi worked hand in hand to rebuild the world's infrastructure and bring food, medicine, power, employment, and education back to the rest of the world.

entries.name: Second Holy Order Selection Tournament
entries.content:
In 2180, five years after the end of the Crusades, the dimensional prison walls that sealed Justice unexpectedly begin to erode away. Fearing the threat would be released from her seal, The United Nations quickly decided to organize an international fighting tournament to see who was worthy of defeating Justice for good, where the winner who defeats Justice will be rewarded a prize: The victor gets to make a "single wish... any wish at all".

At the end of the tournament, Testament appears to the winner (officially, it is Sol, but this varies depending on the character played as), revealing that they hosted the tournament, as a front to revive Justice, and fights the winner, saying "All that's required is the blood of one more sacrifice!" However, they themselves are defeated, and they use their own blood as the sacrifice. Justice is freed from her prison, but promptly killed by the winner.

In Normal Mode of the game, all contestants fight Justice on the last stage, but canonically she is defeated by Sol Badguy and other Gears permanently lose their leader.

The tournament itself is much later revealed to have been a farce orchestrated by the Conclave in order to take control of Justice.

entries.name: Area 42
entries.content:
Area 42 is a location in the Guilty Gear world.

A city of water with frequent reports of spirit discoveries. It has a fantastical appearance, but is closed to diplomatic relations, and very few know of the interior conditions. Recently, limited areas have been opened to the public, and interest as a tourist area has risen. It has developed a unique culture, and some rumors say that the residents have special abilities.

entries.name: Ajatar Hunting Ground
entries.content: It is described as a stage located deep in a dense forest filled with ancient statues. The region is Illyria (possibly Finland)

entries.name: AD. 2172
entries.content: AD. 2172 is a location in the Guilty Gear world, appearing as Order-Sol's battle stage in the Guilty Gear XX titles. The battle takes place in a unnamed battlefield during the Crusades.

entries.name: 12-Dimensional Flux Observatory
entries.content: The 12-Dimensional Flux Observatory is a place related with the Independent Airborne State of Zepp. It is described as place where the blizzard never stops.

entries.name: A Happy Family
entries.content:
A place that defies the laws of physics filled with victorian furniture and architecture.

The place itself is a referance to Golconde by Rene Magritte

entries.name: Jeon Ryok Residence
entries.content:
The Jeon Ryok Residence is a location in the Guilty Gear world, being both Kum Haehyun's family estate and her battle stage. It is also her workplace, functioning as a hospital.

It is in Korea.

entries.name: Japanese Colony
entries.content:
Japanese Colony, usually shortened to just the Colony, is a recurring stage and major location in the Guilty Gear world. There are several "colonies" in different major countries around the world, but only the name of one of them is known: the colony of Miyabi, located near the Mediterranean Sea in the United Kingdoms of Illyria. Ogre Valley is part of this colony.
The birthplace of May, Baiken and Anji Mito, it also serves as Chipp Zanuff's ninja training ground.

entries.name: Japan
entries.content:
Japan is a region and former country that plays a significant part in the history of the Guilty Gear world. The island nation was destroyed in 2074 by Justice on the very day she declared war on humanity.

The few survivors of this calamity, referred to as the Japanese, were all put into protective custody in colonies around the world. Their spirituality display anomalous reactions to supernatural energy, showing a natural affinity for using the ki element.

During the 20th century, Japan enjoyed a massive economic boom and became one of the world's leading economic powers, but political unrest in the 21st century led to an economic collapse. It was then that disaster struck.

Presumably on September 2, 2074, a Gear Project facility on the U.S. was testing the command-type Gear, Justice, when the unknown entity from the Dawn of Revival made contact with Justice, tried to give itself life using her, and copied her DNA data. Concurrently, at least 388 people in Japan started to mutate, with the victims suddenly bursting in agony, transforming into massive and unrecognizable living bomb creatures. Afraid that in an hour the Earth would no longer be a human world, That Man had his team switch Justice over to manual override and fired a maximum output Gamma Ray at Japan. It hit the area between the Korean peninsula and the Japanese islands, completely obliterating the country in an instant, leading to the "Black Sunrise".

Few Japanese survived the ordeal and were gathered by the United Nations in colonies protected by magical barriers. The general public were made to believe that the Japanese were to be viewed as "national treasures" and special citizens who must be protected. In truth, genetic modification was observed, and the colonies were a form of quarantine. Only a select few individuals were aware of this, with the governments in charge of the colonies steadily supplying a vaccine that would retard the changes.

In October 21, 2187, Ramlethal Valentine hides in the lone island that remained after the country's obliteration and declares war on the entire world per her Mother's orders. After a week there Ramlethal is confronted by several people, until a team made up of her own sister Elphelt, Sol Badguy, Ky Kiske, and his son Sin take her into custody upon the Cradle's activation.

entries.name: Illyria Castle
entries.content:
Illyria Castle is the workplace of the First King of the United Kingdoms of Illyria, a position currently held by Ky Kiske, and is located in the kingdom's capitol.

The Royal Court is set in a raised balcony, with a large fouyer standing bellow in the background, where water flows from large pillars addorned with red pipes, a center fountain featuring a rose sculpture. The raised part is connected by two staircases, Rose-headed angel statues hold scales above them. The main balcony is fenced off with iron bars and rope posts, and is adorned with statues of babies holding vases, where rose bushes grow.

entries.name: Hell
entries.content:
Hell is a recurring location in the Guilty Gear world, being Zato-ONE, Eddie and Venom's battle stage in the Guilty Gear X and XX entries.

The stage as a whole has a surreal athmosphere in all its incarnations. The original version in Guilty Gear X serves as the subboss stage, and the battle against Testament takes place on a cliff with a central skull-shaped rock, and a bridge leading to a blocked door guarded by a mounted skeleton. The background is a large purple vortex, with a series of castles on floating ground formations strething to the horizon, and closer to the foreground many tomb-like structures are fused with the rock formations.

Guilty Gear XX sees the stage in a more monochromatic, desaturated blue tone. The buildings are mostly gone, with only the floating islands remaining. At the battleground, skeletons periodically rise up, stand arround, and break down once again. This version of the stage is instead associated with Eddie.

Λ Core sees a more traditional version of hell, featuring a large sea of blood adorned with tombstones, and the ground itself has a largely fleshy look, with bloodstained and cracked tombstones to the right of the battle area. The background are upside down ruined buildings that rise from the mist and a glowy orange sky, with more fog rising up the horizon. This version serves as the stage for both Eddie and Venom.

entries.name: Heaven
entries.content:
Heaven is a recurring location in the Guilty Gear world, appearing as Justice's stage since the original Guilty Gear.

Heaven is the final boss stage of Guilty Gear. It features a large stairway leading to a gateway with a broken door. The stairs are draped in red and golden carpet, and heavily engraved pillars and archways sit on both sides. The background is cloudy, with a bright light emanating from above in the center. Large crystals float besides the archways, with creatures seemingly imprisoned inside them; due to the nature of the stage and its respective fighter, these may be powerful inactive Gears, and their crystals may be manifestations of their dimensional prisons. Guilty Gear X features the exact same stage, only with remade graphics.

In Guilty Gear XX, The stage is under despair, with the archways ruined and its broken pieces scattered arround the carpet, which is now dusty.
