Due to her family's strict position against women holding positions of power, Haehyun was forced to control her robot Jonryoku and only a very few people know her true identity. From a young age, she began offering her services as a Tuner at a high price. To each of the countries she travelled, she collected a piece of the chain on Jonryoku's right arm.

At some point, Haehyun befriended Johnny, who is one of the few who know her identity, although the circumstances in which they met are unknown.

Haehyun receives a call from Johnny requesting her to rendezvous at the Japanese Colony in order to investigate the disturbances there. After treating a patient, she departs from her home, and Da-Eum and her many handmaidens bid her farewell. She arrives earlier than Johnny and Faust, and begins her thorough investigation. When Johnny arrives, she asks Leo Whitefang to let Johnny go free and explains the situation. Leo agrees to her request. Via Johnny's com, Haehyun is able to talk to Faust, who asks to be informed of any changes while he searches for a cure.

She shows May her true identity as she is one of Johnny's girls. Later on, Johnny is worried for Haehyun's safety, but she is willing to help nevertheless because he asked, and they hug. As the residents become ill, Haehyun is worried that they may not have enough time to treat them all. May gives Haehyun an small anchor as a good luck charm and "thank you", and then leaves to find the colony's "power spot", telling Haehyun to eat something as she has been skipping meals.

Haehyun receives her delivery from Jam Kuradoberi, and they talk about small efforts. Leo calls to inform that the problem is not the residents themselves, but the world. May then returns alongside Baiken with a solution. Baiken takes Haehyun and May to a sacred tree infused with the ki of her people during generations. During the crisis to stop the Universal Will, Haehyun uses the massive amount of ki in the tree to control the Information Flares, while Baiken, May and Answer protect her from the Phalanx. Haehyun holds off for about 40 minutes until harmony is restored when the Illyrian main team defeats Ariels and Justice becoming one with Jack-O' Valentine.

entries.name: Ky Kiske
entries.content:
Ky Kiske is a character in the Guilty Gear world and Sol Badguy's rival. A former member of the Sacred Order of Holy Knights during the Crusades, Ky is a charismatic swordsman who possesses a strong sense of justice and piety, which sustain and guide him through all manner of shaking uncertainties.

Ky is a handsome young man with blond hair and blue eyes. His hair has grown in the timeline of the series, to the point where he sports a ponytail in the Xrd games, although he goes back to a short hairstyle in Strive.

His classic outfit is a loosely-fitting, blue base version of the white uniform worn by the Sacred Order of Holy Knights that consists of white trousers and shirt below a white longcoat; its knee-length front resembles a blue cross and has a white elbow-length cape. It is fastened together by a belt buckle inscribed with the word "HOPE". Ky invariably wears fingerless gloves, either black or blue. In Xrd, he returns to a modified Holy Order uniform, much more form-fitting than before. In casual settings, he is shown to favor collared shirts and trousers, seen in artwork and After Story A.

In Overture, he sports instead a elaborate rolled-up longcoat with two big belts as well as a blue cloak, while keeping his color scheme. In Strive, his outfit consists of simple dark blue trousers and dark brown boots, a single-sleeved V-neck dark blue shirt with lapels, a cape-like white jacket over his shoulders, and blue gloves with metal plates on the backhand. Attached to his brown waistbelts is a scabbard wherein he keeps the Thunderseal sheathed. Both his outfits in Xrd and Strive have the phrase "Nothing can be done without hope" and the Illyricum symbol throughout.

Ky is a religious man, the adjective describing both his devotion to God, as well as his commitment to the ideals of justice, order, and honor. Of a straightforward and serious personality, Ky is kind-hearted, charismatic, honest, diligent, polite, and believes in fair play. He is also chivalrous, being known to hold back against female opponents, and is utterly dedicated to protecting the weak. On the other hand, Ky can be notoriously inflexible and is easily disgusted by those who disturb the peace, having a complex about freedom even if he doesn't realize it. He is also a "hot-blooded fool", prone to taking rash actions when angered.

While others may mock Ky for his idealism (especially Sol), he has the determination to live life according to what he believes in. His dogged pursuit for justice and fairness has upset more than a few in power, as he is willing to confront his superiors if he believes them to be corrupt. Ky himself knows that his idealistic dreams can never come true, but he will try regardless for the sake of others he cares for.

Although Ky's strong beliefs once tended to color his moral world black and white, realizing that his 'justice' was limited to human convenience and that no single truth governed everything was a significant blow to his identity. Becoming king prior to Overture also made him lose some of his zeal—his view has since broadened significantly, and has learned to see the world from the perspective of others. Initially conflicted by the appointment, the throne made Ky lose the old shine he had as a youth, but he has since increasingly defied conventions, being the "problem child" according to Leo.

Ky is firmly committed to the public good and to bringing hope to others, and treasures peace above all. However, he was forged by war; such that Justice once remarked that Ky had the "eyes of someone who knew nothing yet but battle". Once a merciless enemy to all Gears, he actively wishes to move on from the "killing machine" that he was during the Crusades, and leave his hatred behind. Although Ky's skills remain as sharp as back then, his sense of honor prevents him from using war-time tactics in duels. Is it also due to such a change in his personality these days, his iconic rivalry with Sol was softened to where Ky himself reflected on the lofty aspects of it.

A skilled fighter, Ky is stated to be a talented swordsman and a genius magic practitioner. He is adept at performing all five forms of elemental magic, but prefers to use lightning, which is said to be the most difficult to control. He has impressed the expert Dr. Paradigm by quickly figuring out a blessing that protects himself and others from the Vizuel's foreign Divine Steps and magic, and is somehow able to enchant his sword with Absolute Defense: Felion despite its authorization restrictions during his battle with I-No.

His weapon of choice is the Thunderseal, an instroment which concentrates and amplifies lightning magic, but requires tremendous physical and mental stamina to be wielded. Due to certain events, he is temporarily forced to replace it with the Aquila and Magnolia Éclair swords; however, his control over lightning remains the same.

Considered a "fearsome enemy", his skill was deemed valuable enough by the P.W.A.B. to be imitated via the Robo-Ky series. At age 15, Ky was famed as a "prodigy" amongst the war-hardened Holy Knights. He claims to use basic Order techniques (where unfairness and deceit are superior), but even so, Ky stood out as a brutally efficient fighter uninhibited by emotion, mercy or honor in the face of monsters—such that Sol himself was fearful of Ky's prowess on the battlefield during the Crusades. In one account, Justice was once forced to retreat by Ky, and noted afterwards that mankind was "blessed with much greater skills as a fighting species than mere Gears". Ky does not generally employ such tactics, however, and seeks to best opponents fairly in his duels.

Due to unknown reasons, Ky has acquired the pure Gear cells of Justice, also called the "blood of Juno". At will, he can regenerate fatal wounds in mere seconds, and his strength vastly increases. Ky's hair (like Sin's) keeps growing at a rapid pace, and Elphelt can use her "mysterious power" to locate him. In Xrd, only his eye turned red, but three weeks later, in Strive, Ky is able to use his own version of Dragon Install, although only a portion of him, centering around his eye, transforms. Whether or not he can still be considered human is unknown.

entries.name: Ky Kiske History
entries.content:
Born circa 2157, Ky lost his mother to the Crusades at a young age. Half a year later after her death, during a Gear attack Ky decided he would no longer run and told Commander Kliff Undersn of the Sacred Order of Holy Knights that he wanted to join. As Ky had no fighting skills, Kliff told the young Ky to survive for five years and to come back then if he really wanted to fight. Ky ran away as ordered, but he officially joined the Order in 2167 at age 10. By age 15, Ky was recognized as a "prodigy swordsman". He became a source of inspiration to other knights, such as Leo Whitefang, and often challenged his comrades to duels to hone skills together.

Around 2172, Ky was made a battalion captain, with Sol Badguy assigned under his command. One day, Ky challenged Sol to a duel; aware of Ky's battlefield prowess, Sol was prepared to go all out, but Ky fought Sol fairly—thinking he was human—and lost. However, Sol interpreted it as Ky not taking him "seriously". In turn, Sol's personality and usual disregard for Ky's orders led to a growing tension between the two.

In 2173, sometime after the Battle of Rome, Ky caught Sol during the act of stealing the Fireseal, but Sol defeated him once again and got away. Ky was to follow suit, but Kliff stopped him and went to speak with Sol himself, leaving Ky with a score to settle. Entrusting the future to both Sol and Ky, Kliff decided to retire and Ky, aged 16, was given leadership of the Order. As a symbol of his new status, Ky was granted the Thunderseal by Kliff, in acknowledgement of his numerous heroic feats in service to the Order and to humanity as a whole.

In 2175, Kliff challenged Justice to one last battle, and Ky stepped in to save him, pushing Justice to retreat. Ky pursued her trail only to find her weakened amidst flames—which was, unbeknownst to him, Sol's work—, and thus ordered all support units to engage and seal Justice in a dimensional prison, bringing the war to an end. The Order was dissolved by the end of the year, but Ky continued his life of public service by entering the International Police Force, where he was promoted to the rank of captain.

In 2180, one day while on duty, the Second Holy Order Selection Tournament is announced. Permission to shed blood during matches, an absurdly large grand prize, and talk of Justice's resurrection make Ky suspicious of a conspiracy. He thus dons the Order's uniform for the first time in five years and decides to enter.

During the tournament, Justice is freed by Testament, but is ultimately defeated by Sol and Ky. Before her death, Justice speaks to Ky. Ky says that evil has no place in their world, but she rejects that label. Born a slave and a weapon, she lived for her assigned role: she was created to kill, and so she did, for that is "justice". Ky says that justice is order, what God ordains and wishes for. Justice wonders if his unwavering faith in the concept would continue if he met That Man, who is still alive. Ky wants to know more, but she dies, leaving Ky to ponder if he was doing the right thing.

In 2181, Ky receives word of a Gear who doesn't wish to harm humans. Questioning his concept of justice and his belief that all Gears are evil since the tournament, Ky is dispatched to the Forest of Demons to investigate those responsible for the announcement. He finds Dizzy, with whom he discusses the meaning of power. Letting himself be defeated, Ky assures Dizzy that there are humans who can handle her powers, and lets her go as a mob closes in on them. Yet, as a result of his defeat, a huge reward was offered for her capture.

In one path, Ky tells Dizzy that the outside world is waiting for her, yet she worries she will be a burden if she leaves; Ky counters that living itself is a burden on others, and offers to teach her how to live as a 'human'. In another, Ky is detected by Robo-Ky and engages in a fight with him, but even after Ky won the battle the robot insists on pursuing him. In his third path, Ky defeats Sol in a duel, and jokingly says he should supervise Sol's training as the two of them are battered and tired.

Ky returns to his normal duties, but two weeks later, Slayer intervenes in Ky's encounter with Venom and shows him the latest bounty list, targeting Japanese outside the Colony. In one path, he strikes a truce with Johnny to find whoever is behind the bounties. In another, Ky after cornering Robo-Ky upon realizing he was being blamed for their actions, defeats a swarm of the robots sent by the Post-War Administration Bureau as he ponders about their motives. In the third, Ky finds Sol after defeating I-No; Ky forcefully inquires about That Man and requesting to bring in I-No on behalf of the police force, but Sol refuses to answer, calling Ky a "spoiled brat" for not considering the consequences of his 'justice' while telling him matters are deeper than beyond what he can manage as a law-abider; Sol then goes away, leaving Ky in the dark.

As he ponders the reality of justice, Ky runs after the P.W.A.B. and investigates one of its branches. In one path, he fights Sol to prove he can handle the organization alone, but Sol wins yet again and Ky decides to let him be. He takes shelter at the Grove until Dizzy, who is there to visit to Testament, loses control of Necro and Undine due to Crow's Justice copy. After he retreats, Dizzy asks Ky to help her find out more about her origins. Ky agrees, but before that, he duels Sol to settle their score once for all. Ky loses, but decides to no longer pursue Sol and reunites with Dizzy. In the other, Ky assists Johnny in attacking the P.W.A.B. branch.

At one point, Dizzy amicably parted with the Jellyfish Pirates and moved in with Ky, helping him out with house chores as he became Chief of the IPF. It wasn't long before they fell in love. Because of the lack of official records and her concealed identity, they could not get officially married, but Ky nevertheless proposed to Dizzy and they pledged their love for each other.

After being together for about a year, their son Sin was born. While Ky loved his wife and son, he was also filled with guilt: the "sin" of loving a Gear, but also Dizzy and Sin being forced to live in hiding. The downcast Ky avoided eye-contact with Sin, which made his son wonder if Ky even cared for them. Sin soon started to hate Ky, refusing to call him "dad" as he grew up.

When Sin was six months old, after two of the Illyrian kingdoms were established, Ky was invited to meet the United Nations' Conclave, who told Ky he was to participate in the upcoming elections. Although he wanted the position as king to change the world for the better—for Dizzy and Sin—, Ky declined to be their puppet, yet they knew about his wife. Not knowing what to do, Ky's turmoil came to a breaking point. He went to church to pray, so Dizzy called Sol to help Ky out. Sol provoked Ky into fighting; he was losing so a frightened Sin told Sol to stop for Dizzy's sake, and Ky was moved to tears at his son's gesture. Ky and Dizzy then entrusted Sin's care to Sol in order to keep him safe. Ky was soon elected as the First King, ruler of the capitol, Europe and a portion of the African continent.

In 2186, like other Gears before her, Dizzy undergoes sublimation but Ky converts the Thunderseal to prevent her from disappearing, but in his desperation, he "rushes" the spell and is unable to release the seal afterwards. He would have his men investigate the cause, but the capital is soon attacked by the Vizuel. Ky immediately issues a bounty on Sol to summon him, but the battle ends with his guards killed and Ky himself is sealed by That Man.[note 3]

He is freed days later by Sol, Sin, Izuna and Dr. Paradigm. Sol asks Ky if Dizzy is safe, but Ky doesn't respond right away, mourning the loss of his subjects; Sin lashes out, calling him a "shitty king" who can't protect anything, and storms out. Ky shows them Dizzy's state, and Paradigm realizes that Justice's cells are the "key" Valentine needs to enter That Man's Cube, and says Dizzy should be destroyed to protect the world. Ky vehemently refuses, declaring his love for her and shocking Paradigm, and revealing that Sin is his son. The castle is then sieged by Gears, and Ky and Paradigm stay to protect Dizzy while Sol and Izuna go rescue Sin.

During the battle, Ky helps Paradigm undo the Gears' brainwashing, his compassion moving the doctor. Ky then leads his men into battle against the Vizuel army in Bel Canto Valley so that Sol can enter the Backyard. Before leaving, Sol punches Sin into staying with Ky. Ky apologizes to Sin, acknowledging he wasn't a good father, while Sin reflects that he will protect Ky because he is irreplaceable to Dizzy. They fight side by side, but Ky—who just wanted to see how much his son had grown—lets Sin go help Sol; Sin leaves, saying Ky doesn't need to talk so "formally" if he wants to act like a dad.

Ky reunites with everyone after Sol kills Valentine and returns from the Backyard. Back at the castle, Ky invites Paradigm to remain so that he can study Dizzy's state. During an emergency session of the General Assembly to discuss the Baptisma 13 incident, Ky opens the conference by announcing his wish for human-Gear coexistence in Illyria, causing an outrage. Days later, Paradigm questions the wisdom of it, but Ky thinks that unity will be necessary in wake of the "merciless apocalypse" threat.

In 2187, Elphelt Valentine warns Ky about her sister's future threat. She is imprisoned as a precaution, but Ky—wary of the Conclave—takes her from Illyria aboard the Royal Fleet One. On October 21, Ramlethal Valentine indeed declares war on the entire world, and Ky hires Sol, and Sin, to help stop Ramlethal. Upon the Cradle's activation on October 28, as everything Elphelt predicted comes to pass, Ky releases her in spite of Leo Whitefang's veto, and she helps them take Ramlethal into custody. The next day, after a Cradle apparition, Leo advices Ky to go to Zepp. Meanwhile, Sin tries to befriend Ramlethal, and questions Sol's lonely worldview. En route to Zepp, Ky asks Sol if he only cares about his revenge and nothing else, insisting that Sol has a future, and that he, Dizzy and Sin will welcome Sol when he is done. Shortly after, they meet with Gabriel and Zato-ONE; the latter reveals the Conclave's plan to resurrect Justice.

After Paradigm and That Man's allied ambush on the Cradle fails, and the latter is imprisoned away by Bedman, Ramlethal finally talks: the Conclave will use St. Elmo's Fire and Illyria Castle to awaken Justice. On November 4, during the capital's evacuation, Ky and Sin are reunited with Dizzy (whom Paradigm unsealed while they were gone), and Sin finally calls Ky "Dad". During the operation, Leo, Sin and Ky defend the control room from the Opus. Ky easily takes care of the hostiles in his area, but Axus ambushes Ky, shooting him several times. However, Ky—with a crimson left eye—gets to his feet and kills Axus. In the aftermath of the Conclave's defeat, Elphelt, forced by her programming, reveals that everything went according to her mother's design before she and Justice are abducted.

The day after, a downcast Ky inspects the self-repairing Thunderseal and admits to Dizzy that he is feeling helpless. Dizzy reminds him about the day they first met, and Ky thanks her. Later that day, Ky contacts Zepp to help him investigate the Conclave's Opera House. On November 7, he shares his feelings with Potemkin to put him at ease, until Chipp Zanuff interrupts them and warns Ky that the Universal Will may be human. Days later, he shows St. Maximus Ariels proof of the Opus' danger; he remembers Chipp's words and asks Ariels if she loves humanity, but she refrains from answering.

After Sol returns to the capital, Ky and Sol reflect on their past rivalry (as Ky is busy filling out papers), with the latter surprised at Ky's indifference—in contrast on his stubborn insistence to defeat Sol in a duel—towards his past as Frederick. Ky says he is interested, but that Sol's future matters much more, tying it to his job of bringing "hope" to others and acknowledging Sol as a friend and offering him whiskey hidden under his desk he never bothered to drink as a sign of such acknowledgement. After a meeting to discuss the Information Flares with Zappa and Faust, Ky, Sol, Leo and Paradigm meet with That Man and Jack-O' Valentine, and learn about the Absolute World, That Man's motives, and Ariels being the Universal Will. Learning that a Phalanx was involved in the Scandiva incident, Ky makes up his mind about Ariels.

As per their plans, Ky and Leo confront Ariels at the celebration of victory, during which she announces her identity to the world before retreating; Ky obtains the XYZ from her, but she erases her signal. Zappa and Randy manage to locate her, however, and leaving the capitol's defense to Dizzy and their allies, Ky departs alongside Sol, Sin and Jack-O' to the Celestial Altar aboard Johnny's Gullinkambi Dark. During the journey, Sin brings up if Dizzy is related to Sol, Ky is horrified as he realizes that Sol may be his father-in-law. Against all odds, they are victorious: Ariels is defeated by Sol, Ramlethal turns up alive with Raven to help, Elphelt is freed, and despite Daryl's attempt to destroy Justice (and Sol and Jack-O' along with her), Jack-O' and Justice merge thanks to Axl Low and a weakened Ariels.

After the battle, Ky and Dizzy invite Sin, Elphelt and Ramlethal to rest at their estate, although Ky isn't sure how long they all can stay as he intends to make his marriage public, but Elphelt brings news of Dizzy being publicly praised for helping defend the capitol. Yet, Ky ends up horrified as they discuss Sol's place in the family. At that moment, Sol arrives with the intent to fight. Ky and Sol take a walk, with the latter asking if their score is truly settled. Ky says it is, but Sol claims Ky was never "serious" in their fights, having never unleashed his killing prowess used against the Gears during the Crusades which made Sol fear for his own life (which resulted in him only being annoyed for years to come due to only crossing swords since their very first duel). Ky admitted to him that he never saw Sol as a "monster" to be slain in the first place as opposed to someone to be beaten in a fair duel as he refuses to follow through with the request. Sol however, then calls Dizzy a monster to goad Ky; angered, Ky fights dirty and wins easily, ending with Sol lying down on the ground. Sol then asked about the tactics the Holy Knights used against the Gears during the Crusades, and upon hearing Sol say that he wanted to learn how humans can face monsters back then, Ky then pieces together the purpose of their scuffle: Sol is learning how prepare for his final showdown with That Man. Ky upon understanding Sol's conundrum, decides to help him with his issue.

Three weeks later, while Ky is officially "out on an expedition" for saying he planned to make his family public at G4, I-No breaks into Ariels' containment cell. Ky, then Daryl and Leo, inspect the site, learning that I-No took something from Ariels. On Daryl's suggestion, Ky tells Sol to return to the castle; despite Leo's concerns, Ky decides to try and capture I-No so that G4 can proceed. Upon Sol's arrival, Ky gives him an Iseo permit that he requested, then tries to hire him to capture I-No, and informs Sol of Vernon's summons and That Man, Asuka R. Kreutz's, involvement in G4.

Sol first leaves on a vacation with Jack-O', but after I-No lets herself be captured and an encounter with Happy Chaos, he returns to help Ky interrogate I-No. She reveals nothing; instead, Jack-O' tells the duo of I-No's origins and her being incomplete, likely being after Asuka's Tome of Origin. Whereas Sol departs for the G4 Summit, Ky remains behind and watches as Jack-O' interrogates I-No. Upon the latter's mention of G4, Ky decides to go join Sol at the summit, and has Jack-O' come with him, telling her she can't "save the world" via her sacrifice as she is now. Aboard his airship, Jack-O' asks Ky what he meant earlier, and he says that she—who hasn't had the chance to live just yet—has yet to understand what the world is and also tells her about "necessary frivolities".

They arrive after Sol, Vernon, Asuka and their allied forces regain control of the airborne White House after ejecting Chaos on a escape pod. Ky, Jack-O' and Vernon serve as witnesses to Sol and Asuka settling their score, with the latter removing Sol's "divine seed" and restoring his humanity. Unbeknownst to them, Chaos is still onboard; and he then manages to get a hold of Asuka, who has fused with the real Tome, and restores I-No at his own expense. I-No, now a goddess, easily defeats Sol, Giovanna and Potemkin and then leaves. Jack-O' sees no other option but to sacrifice herself, but Ky asks that she stand back and confronts I-No on his own, in spite of her being all-powerful.

After I-No starts a process with the Tome that will grant mankind the same power she has (which Asuka theorizes will destroy their world), Ky fights her using his own Dragon Install. He is unable to stop her, not even with Axl's help, so Jack-O' tries to turn I-No human at the cost of her own life. However, Sol convinces Jack-O' not to go through with it, planning to use a Spiritas Type 48-powered Outrage to defeat I-No. Ky says he will put the best fight he can, distracting her with some assistance from Axl, and ultimately, Sol is able to hit I-No's weak point thanks to Nagoriyuki's unexpected assistance. With her apparent demise, the crisis is averted; back at the castle, Ky, Leo, Millia and Zato reflect on the incident, and the importance of one's present time. Ultimately, Ky goes back home to Dizzy, Sin, Elphelt and Ramlethal, where they are joined by Testament.

entries.name: Leo Whitefang
entries.content:
Leo Whitefang is a character in the Guilty Gear world. Leo is one of the Three Kings of the United Kingdoms of Illyria, governing over twenty nations in the European and Asian regions of Illyria. Also an accomplished warrior in his own right, he shares a friendly rivalry with Ky Kiske.

Leo is a very tall and somewhat rugged-looking man with shoulder-length, unkempt blond hair, a beard, and blue eyes. The jacket he wears is much more sophisticated than his fellow Kings' outfits as an orange, fur-laced coat bearing several belts and crosses. Each leg of his pants also has a cross to match the jacket. He also wears black fingerless gloves. "Noblesse oblige" and "Ignorance may kill a lion" are written throughout his outfit and weapons.

His Strive design gives him a far more down-to-earth look by changing his color scheme from orange and black to brown. He now wears a simple white open-collared shirt below a black double-breasted waistcoat with rectangular lapels, as well as light-brown flannel trousers. His brown trenchcoat still keeps the light orange fur collar—yet no longer cape-like as before—and fur cuffs.

Leo has a rather boisterous attitude, and is constantly and overwhelmingly intimidating. He can be extremely loud whenever caught off-guard, but in reality, he is an exceptionally cautious person who spares no effort when solving problems, and is serious and level-headed whenever a situation demands it.

At the same time, Leo has far more pride than the average man, and hates losing above all. Leo's pride appears to be a result of his great fighting aptitude, but in his youth it also made him "self-centered" and ready to disregard anybody—which was everyone—he thought was inferior. Meeting Ky humbled Leo, and led him to try and improve himself. While Leo still holds himself in high esteem, and is not shy to praise his own skill when victorious, he is not necessarily arrogant: he is a much harsher critic of himself than he is of anyone else, and if he had to grade himself, he would probably say "C-". In turn, he seems to have developed something of an inferiority complex towards Ky, even if he completely trusts him.

Leo is in the process of building his own personal dictionary, a copy of The Royal Illyrian Dictionary, and tends to redefine words as he sees fit, with actual people and events. For example, he has written his sister's name in the section for "devil."

In terms of combat prowess, Leo has always been proficient in both magic and swordmanship. As a kid and up until he joined the Holy Order, he was "always the best" until he met Ky Kiske; the gap between them made Leo reflect on his skills and incited him to train and work on bettering himself since then. Leo's combat skill and tactical acumen are remarkable, as in one pivotal moment during the Crusades, his unit faced what appeared to be certain death, but Leo's skills allowed them to survive. Regarding magic, Leo isn't particularly versed in the basics of magical theory—at least, in comparison with the likes of Dr. Paradigm, Zappa, Ky and Sol—, but excels in metal shaping spells.

His weapons, twin blades held from the underside, are capable of harnessing powerful energy that can be launched in waves. He is able to shrink them down to a more portable size to be placed on his waist, or they can even take alternate shapes, such as a lion's face in his Windrad des Weltraum technique. His fighting style is unique: He prefers a stance where his back faces the opponent, and holds his twin blades ready to strike at any moment.

entries.name: Leo Whitefang History
entries.content:
Born sometime during the Crusades, Leo was a gifted combatant since he was a kid, and joined the Sacred Order of Holy Knights in the fight against the Gear menace that threatened to drive mankind to extinction. At some point he met the young prodigy Ky Kiske. Fighting together during the war, they would become friends, though Leo would rather call him an "inspiration" instead. Angry at Ky's friendly attitude and superiority in every regard, Leo cheered himself up by writing down Ky's name next to the entry for "bambino" in his dictionary, but changed his arrogant behavior.

At some point, Leo was assigned command of his own unit. Near the end of the war, humanity's strategic point in the Tasmanian Islands was attacked, endangering the perimeter they maintained. On the Order's behalf, Leo led the charge to secure the border. He and his unit faced what appeared to be certain death, but his leadership allowed them to escape and succeed in their endeavor. The war finally came to an end with Justice's sealing in 2175.

In the following years, Leo and Ky's paths seldom crossed, but then the United Kingdoms of Illyria was formally recognized in 2183. Leo was elected as its Second King to oversee the local government of more than twenty nations, his purview being Old Russia and the Middle Eastern states. Months later, Ky was elected as the First King. At some point, Leo was responsible for brokering an alliance with the Federation of China.

In October 21, 2187, Ky departs to confront Ramlethal Valentine on Japan, and Leo assumes command of Illyria Castle's War Room. On October 28, during the tragedy of Babylon as the Cradle dematerializes, Leo gives orders to control the situation, then Ky calls Leo to request his approval in releasing Elphelt Valentine. Leo refuses, but Ky releases her anyway; with her help, they capture Ramlethal. Leo later exchanges information with Colin Vernon.

On October 29, Major Lyle's unit encounters the Cradle and contacts the War Room. Leo orders him to keep a safe distance away until they can analyze it, but Lyle attacks anyway, ending in disaster. Leo, noting a spell involved, sends a recording of the incident to Ky and tells him to contact Zepp. On November 1, Leo receives confirmation from Ky that the Conclave is involved, and agrees to release Dr. Paradigm on Ky's behalf. Following the doctor's explanation about the Cradle, Leo oversees the preparations for their ambush.

On November 2, Leo oversees the operation at the projected target area, and manages to delay Bedman from destroying the last beacon with the help of Johnny. Ultimately, That Man and Sol Badguy destroy the Cradle's barrier, but the attack fails due to the Conclave getting away with Justice's body. Ramlethal then finally reveals their plan of using St. Elmo's Fire to awaken Justice. On November 4, upon evacuating the capital, Leo stays behind and helps guard Paradigm and Dizzy's location with Ky and Sin, while Sol removes Chronus from Justice. Leo, separated from the others during the Opus attack, is assisted by Elphelt, but her programming activates and attacks Leo. In the aftermath, Leo tries to warn the others; although Sol makes Elphelt return to her senses, she and Justice are teleported away by the Universal Will.

After the incident, Leo finds himself buried in paperwork, and reads a strange report from an outpost in Finland. On November 9, after receiving information from Vernon, Leo travels to Miyabi to investigate the Conclave. On November 16, he comes across Faust and Chronus by chance, and tries to capture them but they get away. Two days later, Johnny and May agree to let themselves be "captured" to share intel, but Haehyun Kum intervenes and requests that he let the duo go. Because of her status, Leo concedes. He then learns of a disturbance in the colony; Haehyun vows to investigate and keep him informed.

Back at the capitol, Leo informs Vernon via comm about what happened; in turn, Vernon asks if Sol can be trusted. Leo says that if Ky trusts him, so does he for the time being. After Sol is attacked by a massive Gear, Leo and Paradigm discuss about the correlationship between these events and the Universal Will, when they notice Zappa and Faust at the castle's entrance, and Leo lets them in. With their help, the team ascertains the nature of Information Flares. Sometime later, Leo calls Sol (having learned from Ramlethal's reports about his past) and orders him to save the world, treating him as a human, and not a god, out of concern; while Sol says he will seal Justice only to save Elphelt, Leo is satisfied.

Later on, Leo allows Ramlethal and Sin to check Scandiva where Elphelt's ID has been detected, but it is a trap and Ramlethal goes MIA. Leo, Ky, Sol and Paradigm then meet with That Man and Jack-O' Valentine, who tell them of the Absolute World and that Ariels is the Universal Will. Though he is initially outraged at the idea, Leo agrees to go with Ky and confront her at the celebration of victory, durinig which she shows her true self, in order to obtain a blood sample and track her signal. After Zappa and Randy locate her, Leo takes command of the War Room while Ky, Sol, Sin and Jack-O' are to ambush Ariels at the Celestial Altar. Daryl then calls Leo to relay his contingency plan in case Jack-O's fusion with Justice doesn't work out: destroying them with Collider Cannons. Determined to not let Sol die, Leo tries to have Daryl removed from his post as Third King, but Ky refuses. Ultimately, Sol and Jack-O' survive, with her completing the merge thanks to Axl Low and a weakened Ariels.

Days later, Leo is at the War Room to help deal with the aftermath, reluctant to return to his own jurisdiction due to the vast amount of paperwork amassed in his absence. He then receives a call detailing That Man turning himself in to the U.S. government and tells Ellsworth to turn on the radio to confirm That Man's public surrender.

Three weeks later, a time-travelling witch criminal known as I-No invaded the Illyrian Castle prison and taking out Leo's security cameras to avoid Leo and his allies from finding out what she is after, or rather, whom she unseal from Ariels' body. When Daryl takes interest in researching I-No, Leo give his fellow king about her past criminal information.

As I-No is planning something worst soon, at time when G4 occurs in U.S.A. where the Gear Maker, Asuka volunteers as well, and the government wants to invite Sol as a guest knight, Leo becomes worry about the summit's world peace might end up failure, due to I-No is still on the run.

When I-No suddenly turn herself in, after she and her associate, Happy Chaos destroyed the center building of Illyria to unseal Nagoriyuki and force him to work for them, while Chaos and Nagoriyuki escapes, Leo is enlisted by Daryl to work with former assassins Millia Rage (now the new leader of Post-War Administration Bureau) and Zato-ONE (whose Assassin's Guild is now a reformed espionage group), much to Leo's displease, due to their past records. While investigating and tighten the White House's security system before G4 occurs, Leo, Millia, Daryl and Zato discover a mystery "black box" within the building, and Illyria was one of the military industries involved on the building's construction, not even the current president Vernon aware of this. As Daryl and Sol arrive at the White House, U.S.A. and join G4, while Ky and Jack-O are on the way to catch up with them soon, Leo is listening to Zato and Millia's redemption. However they are too late to realize to stop Chaos from hacking the Illyrian's computer network, and the White House is now completely compromise, just as the Illyrian computer immediately shows the hologram of White House. When Chaos immediately activate nuclear missile to destroy across the countries, Leo orders many officers in security room to find a way to prevent, but the world's leaders (including Daryl) who are currently held hostages by Chaos immediately being forced into self-destruct the missiles, while Zato manage to prevent the missile from being destroyed.

When Chaos activated the White House area's true form as an airship called Tir na nOg, preventing Sol and Vernon from escaping, Leo have no choice to immediately calls Goldlewis Dickinson at Pentagon about what Millia and Zato found on the airship White House. Leo's warning from Millia and Zato’s intel about the White House airship being not an aircraft becomes an example of the American Firefly 3 Air Force jet being destroyed by its security weapons. When an airplane TH10-8 just passed by the White House airship, the PWAB co-operate with Zepp to keep an eye on the airship, until a rescue plane arrive. Thanks to Chief of Staff Erica Bartholomew, Leo and his allies can now uncover "black box"'s mystery. While the White House is now above Neo Phoenix, Leo and his allies are relieve that Daryl manage to make amends with Chaos to let him and the world's leaders free and secure to a rescue plane, barring Sol, Vernon and Asuka, including Giovanna. Before Daryl escape with the leaders safely, he manage to implement secret transmission beneath a cup of cold coffee, allowing Leo and his allies to further uncover White House's PEOC. When Chipp arrive at Pentagon, just as the White House went to Old Mexico instead, Leo and his allies learns Chaos' true plan after stealing Asuka's Tome of Origin for I-No. Just as Chipp transmitting communications on each three bases through Anji, who is at a ruin site where Chaos forcefully freed Nagoriyuki, Leo and his allies are shocked to learn that Chaos is in fact the real That Man, the true mastermind behind the ongoing tragic events Justice’s Crusades, with Asuka being used as a scapegoat for the cause, and only Nagoriyuki who knows Chaos' weakness.

When Goldlewis hesitant to sacrifice the White House with missiles, at time after Chaos defeats Asuka from controlling the White House airship, just as Nagoriyuki defeats Giovanna, Leo threaten the secretary not to do so, or Illyria will use their own missiles to counterattack US', in which Goldlewis eventually agrees. When both Asuka, Vernon and Sol manage to get rid of Chaos through trapping him inside PEOC escape pod, instead of escaping from him, Leo and his allies celebrates. Just as Ky and Jack-O arrive at White House, and Asuka revert Sol back to a human known as Frederick Bulsara, Leo informs Ky that the U.S. soldier apprehended Chaos, on behalf of Daryl and Leo's believes on Sol. However, an injured Giovanna happen to talk about not keeping Vernon's cartoony high-ranked badge, making Leo realize something is not right and checking on White House and soldiers' security cameras. Upon re-learning Chaos' shapeshifting and brainwashing abilities, and Giovanna confirms that Chaos stole a jacket of Udos, a new agent, instead of Chief Stryper's, Leo realize that the real Chaos disguising as a brainwashed Udos and still inside the White House, meaning Sol's detransformation back to human is on a bad timing. When Chaos reveals the real Tome had been fusing with Asuka and use its power to fuse himself with I-No into a singular god-like being. Due to I-No's magic affects many bases' war table computers, showing her god-like silhouette form, Leo and many people who sees her in that form are unable to stop their tears from keep dropping out unexpectedly, until Sol destroys I-No, thanks to Vernon, Jack-O, Asuka, Axl Low, Giovanna, Potempkin, Dragon Installed Ky, and a redeemed Nagoriyuki. Sometimes after the incident ends, and G4 becomes success and enacting peaceful era, Leo, Ky, Millia and Zato are discussing about I-No's true desire, and express that present requires past, future, hope and foundation, as well as people's inner-selves like theirs, something which I-No lacked of. After the discussion, Leo is last seen with Dr. Paradigm, with the former is struggling doing paperworks he received from other world's leaders across the country.

entries.name: Leopaldon
entries.content:
Leopaldon is a mysterious character that has only appeared in Guilty Gear Isuka as the boss of the game's Arcade Mode. It's an entity composed of a dog fused with an ancient Gear and controlled by the dog's owner, a drum-beating sorcerer. It's unclear whom the name belongs to, but it most likely refers to either the dog, the Gear, or both.

The Gear is a massive, white-scaled creature with red eyes, muscular limbs, and brown fur that covers its hands and nether regions (with a tuft of fur sticking out its backside, which acts as its tail). It sports black tattoos on its shoulders, tan bandages around its forearms, and black open-toed boots on its feet. Its massive mouth is full of big yellow teeth and brown threads connecting its gums to its lips. As the sorcerer and his dog reside within the Gear's mouth, the Gear keeps its mouth perpetually open wide. The only time it's shown with its mouth not like this is in its introduction animation, where it pops out of a pile of snow shaped like a Greek head bust, and is crocodilian and reptilian in shape, making it resemble a dinosaur in someway.

The sorcerer's pet is a brown-furred, black-nosed dog. On its head is a piece of black headwear reminiscent of a gimp mask. On the parts of the headwear where the eyeholes would be are two red ornaments that look like ball gags. Since it's fused with the Gear, its head is the only part of its body that's seen most of the time. The only time its full body is shown is in Leopaldon's win animation, where the Gear kneels and the dog momentarily defuses with it to pant.

The sorcerer is a red-eyed humanoid clad in black armor that perpetually beats on a big brown drum.

The Gear has no personality, being a corpse the dog fused with and the sorcerer keeps perpetually animated. Because of this, it merely serves as the "body" of Leopaldon. It's only real characteristic is its ability to cause destruction on a massive scale, just like its fellow Gears.

The dog bears little more than the usual characteristics a common dog has. It is, however, the "mind" of Leopaldon, as it's fused with the Gear and the way the Gear moves hint the dog's using the Gear's body as its own. Because of this, it's likely the character the player's actually fighting—and the one that actually bears the name "Leopaldon"—is the dog. The fact Leopaldon's in-game portrait often closes in on the dog further supports this theory.

All that's known about the sorcerer is he's a good man always trying to do the right thing, using the Gear's powers to help those in need. It's unknown why he perpetually beats on a drum, but since he's Leopaldon's "pilot", it's likely how he keeps the Gear animated.

There is very little information on Leopaldon. Originally a huge white Gear, it is now in a semi-fused state with a brown dog. It should be incapacitated, but it is piloted by a mysterious man, simply called a "sorcerer", who has the ability to steer Gears. The sorcerer himself is not malicious and seems to be using the Gear's abilities to aid people living in the polar regions.

The game's tagline is presented thusly: A new Gear arises, its name Leopaldon. As they threaten to lay waste to the world, everyone prepares to mount their offense. The confrontation takes place in Antarctica, as it is Leopaldon's stage, and he is presumably defeated for good.

Leopaldon is extremely resilient, as the Gear's belly is impervious to all attacks; the game reads all attacks directed there as a Guard. To defeat him, one must attack the sorcerer and his dog; as they're stationed in the Gear's open mouth, they can only be defeated by aerial attacks. He can also be hurt by hitting his back by using a teleportation attack. His main technique are claw swipes, as well as forming walls of ice or fire stones via magic spells.

The giant Gear is thought to be a Megadeath-class Gear, due to its large size and attacks, many of which being extremely powerful and destructive—such as Perfect Rainbow, a laser that is belched from its mouth.

entries.name: May
entries.content:
May is a character in the Guilty Gear world. She is the young-looking and spunky first mate of the Jellyfish Pirates and is utterly dedicated to Johnny, her captain and the man who raised her after she was orphaned during the final years of the Crusades.

May is portrayed in the games as a young girl with brown eyes and waist-length hair, usually tied in a ponytail. Despite the series' chronology spanning seven years, she seems to never age.

Her usual outfit consists of an orange coat, with a skin tight body suit underneath, and big orange boots. She wears an orange pirate tricorn hat and fingerless gloves with silver plating over them. She is seen easily carrying a ship's anchor of about her own size. In the Xrd games, May's waist cape loses the cloth in the front, and her tights are replaced with orange pants. The rest of her design remains relatively the same.

In Strive, she maintains her fingerless gloves, boots as well as her trademark orange pirate hat, but she now wears an orange hooded sweatshirt and black lycra shorts, and carries a beige Chimaki-themed backpack.

May is cheerful and openhearted, but also childish in her way of thinking. Being something of a plucky girl, May uses the pronoun 僕 (boku?), primarily used by boys and young men. Per her own words, all she does is enjoy the simple life with her friends, and her motivations are rather simple: they revolve around protecting her family, the Jellyfish Pirates—going so far as to part ways with them if that means their safety, no matter how much she wants to be with them—, and getting Johnny's attention.

For her captain and savior, May has an intense and abiding love, usually measuring the value of things in relation to Johnny, and often boasts that if it came down to Johnny or the world, she would choose Johnny every time. She is anxious to become a woman so that he might notice her, but so far has met with little success on that front.

A spunky and energetic soul, May likes pranks, and never sweats the small stuff. She believes in taking action first, and thinking later, and oftens drags her friends along with her impulsive behavior. At the same time, her positivity is infectious, and no one can be around her for long without feeling buoyed by her enthusiasm, even if it sometimes gets to the point it becomes exhausting. May also has an irrational fear of bald people or peladophobia, and can sense them from a distance. Because of this, she is wary of Faust, although she does trust his medical expertise.

May is rather powerful herself, and Faust, even before learning that she is Japanese, stated that a great deal of power is hidden within her. May fights with a massive ship's anchor, which she is able to swing with ease despite her small stature, displaying superhuman strength. Regarding magic spells, May is capable of momentarily summoning aquatic animals—such as Mr. Dolphin, the otter Dodomezaki, or the killer whale Mr. Goshogawara—to attack her opponents; some consider summoning to be the ultimate magical skill. Due to her Japanese heritage, May is presumed to have been born with the ability to control the Ki element; however, she has yet to display any overt control over it in comparison with the likes of Chipp, Jam, or Haehyun.

Despite her childish frame and demeanor, May is older than she looks and behaves. Having barely aged during the seven-year time gap between the original Guilty Gear and Guilty Gear Xrd, her real age is a mystery. May once whispers her age to Chipp Zanuff when he assumes she is only a child, making him scream in amazement. Whether or not this is connected to her hidden power or genetics remains to be seen.

entries.name: May History
entries.content:
Born to parents who belonged to one of the colonies, May lost her home and entire family to the Crusades at a young age, and wandered the battlefield afterwards. Her original name, birthday or nationality lost to her, all she would ever remember of her childhood is Johnny whisking her away from the savage battlefield in 2174. Johnny took her in, and named her "May" after the month of endless rain, during which she was found. He gave her a new home aboard the May Ship, and the Jellyfish Pirates became her family. She grew to be a integral member of the crew, and was named first mate.

Throughout the long years of living aboard the airship, May developed a fierce love for Johnny: He was part father figure, part brother, and perhaps even part boyfriend to her. However, one day, in 2180, Johnny—who primarily stole from the well-off to aid those in need—was caught in the act and was incarcerated, and was given a long sentence.

May and her fellow crew members immediately began planning an elaborate breakout. The day before the plan was to commence, April asks if it is too late to change the plan. May learns of the Second Holy Order Selection Tournament, in which the winner gets to make any wish. Thinking they can ask for Johnny to be released, May enters the tournament.

Unbeknownst to May, the tournament is a farce to free Justice from her dimensional prison, but the Gear commander is defeated by Sol Badguy. Even though May doesn't win, Johnny manages to bust himself out of prison. In May's ending, Justice realizes that May is Japanese, but is cut short by the arrival of Johnny and the rest of the crew. When May asks what the Gear had called her, Johnny dismisses Justice's words, and proposes that they celebrate his return instead.

In 2181, May hopes to give Johnny a birthday present, separate from the rest of the crew, but she realizes he doesn't have any money. Hearing of the huge bounty put on a Gear, May heads off to the U.S. to capture her. In one path, May fights Anji Mito, who recognizes her as Japanese. It prompts May to ask Johnny about it, but he blows it off, not wanting to tell her the truth yet. In another path, May manages to reach Dizzy and both fight. May realizes that Dizzy isn't a bad person, and invites her to join the crew, which would be May's "present" to Johnny: a new member.

In truth, it was Johnny who found Dizzy and invited her to join their crew. Having failed to capture her bounty, May returns to find herself a crew mate; although sad at being unable to give Johnny a gift, May contents herself with gaining a friend in Dizzy, teaching her how to survive on a ship.

A few weeks later, I-No attacks the May Ship, denting it, and then knocks Dizzy off the ship in order to lay a trap for Sol. Testament shows up unannounced to visit Dizzy, and attacks May thinking that they were the ones to push Dizzy off the ship. After the fight, the entire crew begins their search for Dizzy.

In one path, May is delayed by Eddie, and Dizzy is nowhere to be found; Potemkin shows up and explains that he took care of the one responsible. In a misunderstanding, May attacks Potemkin and, with April's help, takes Dizzy back to the May Ship. In another path, May subdues Dizzy but, upon their return, they run into Bridget, who believes that Dizzy still has a bounty on her. May remains behind to fight, and explains that Dizzy no longer is a wanted person; May and Bridget thus become friends. In her third path, while May is searching for Dizzy, she runs into Anji, who explains the current status of the Japanese. Back on the May Ship, May tells Johnny that she wants to know about her past. They are interrupted by a Robo-Ky, with Johnny asking the frustrated May if she would like to dance, and May obliges.

Though it is smooth sailing for the crew, May is feeling a little down, having begun to wonder about her past ("...What exactly am I?"). After a visit from Bridget, May and Johnny arrange for Dizzy to visit Testament. However, Dizzy's powers go out of control again and Johnny disappears; leaving Dizzy in Ky Kiske's care, she looks for Johnny. Regardless of choices, May meets Anji. May either goes with Anji to learn more about her ancestry, or Anji advises May that she ask the person she trusts the most. Upon finding Johnny, she asks him, and he reassures May that no matter what happens they are family.

In October 2187, May begins to suffer from strange headaches, and Johnny takes it upon himself to find Faust, leaving May in charge of the May Ship II. After Ramlethal Valentine declares war on entire world, May decides to beat her up as she feels it is the right thing to do, despite her crewmates' worries. On her way to Japan, Chipp Zanuff makes May realize that her friends are worried about her, and then names himself as her chaperone. May is shocked to hear from Ramlethal that she is a "disease" because of her heritage.

Not wanting to cause harm to her family, May runs away from the ship. After getting lost in the Uighur mountains, May is on a bridge when it snaps, but she is saved by Chipp. Following a conversation with Chipp about how families solve their problems together, May finds the courage to face Johnny and the crew. When they are reunited, May apologizes in tears, but everyone is relieved to see her safe. Faust then arrives and gives May some medicine, and advises them to stay away from the colony. Faust's suspicions attract Bedman's attention, who knocks the doctor out. With Chipp staying behind to buy them time, the pirate crew escapes on the May Ship II with the unconscious Faust. Aware of Bedman's existence and the Illyrian efforts, May, Johnny and the crew assist Faust in installing a beacon to ambush the Cradle near the Black Sea.

On November 11, in hopes of finding a cure for May and to investigate the disturbances in the colonies, Johnny arranges to rendezvous there with his old friend, Kum Haehyun, and Faust. A week later, May and Johnny arrive at the colony, where they are almost apprehended by Leo Whitefang. Haehyun intervenes, however, and asks Leo to let them go free, which he agrees to. May later thanks Haehyun for the help; as May is one of Johnny's girls, Haehyun shows May her true identity, surprising May. Johnny soon departs to take care of other business.

Thanks to undergoing suppressive treatment, May doesn't suffer due to the Information Flares but the colony's residents become ill. When Haehyun expresses her concerns about the situation, May gives her a good luck charm—a small anchor made in Russia—as a "thank you" for protecting her parents' former home. Reflecting on her simple life so far, wanting to do something to help prevent the end of the world, May leaves to find the colony's "power spot".

May calls Baiken over and explains about the Universal Will's threat. Baiken takes May and Haehyun to a sacred tree infused with the ki of her people during generations. In the following crisis, May, Baiken and Answer protect Haehyun from the Phalanx while she uses the tree's energy to suppress the Information Flares. They hold off for at least 40 minutes until harmony is restored the moment the Illyrian main team defeats Ariels, which causes the Phalanx soldiers to deactivate, and Justice merges with Jack-O' Valentine.

Three weeks later, May is celebrating alongside April, Johnny, Leap, March doing the laundry, and Augus, having landed the May Ship II somewhere.

entries.name: Millia Rage
entries.content:
Millia Rage is a character in the Guilty Gear world. A former member of the Assassin's Guild, she fights with the skills of her old occupation in search of a better life. Wielding her cursed hair as a weapon, she is able to give it any shape and form that she desires.

Millia has long flowing blonde hair and blue eyes with dark eyelashes. Millia's hair in her in-game stance is seen tied in a ponytail, but given its properties, it changes shape frequently, from cut short to very lengthy, and can take any shape, even that of decorative flowers.

Millia's classic outfit consists of a white blouse with light blue hemlines and a collar that covers the whole of her neck; there are also two straps that run across her collar bone right above her chest. She also wears a leotard under her blouse, padded arms, whole length gloves, and a light blue headband across her forehead and her legs are also bare.

In Xrd, Millia's design has drastically changed, as she now wears a yellow blouse with black hemlines and a large circular pin near the top of her blouse depicting a cat with an "X" over its mouth and eyes with "Curiosity killed the cat" written in cursive on the bottom of the ring around the cat, complete with a matching pillbox hat that has a sign saying "zl-28" and "13", black leggings, white fingerless gloves and peach colored ballet shoes.

In Strive, she now wears a short beige trench coat, with a light orange shawl over her shoulders and a beige fur hat with the Xrd sign attached to it. She wears a P.W.A.B. armband on her left arm, black gloves and a new shade of leggings with black knee-highs boots.

Millia is elegant and calm, but does not hesitate to fight when necessary. Cold and somewhat silent, she was molded by years of assassin conditioning, with an upbringing apparently bereft of much affection. Of serene reactions that show little interest in anything, Millia doesn't feel at disadvantage for being a woman, and makes decisions solely on the basis of cost and benefit. Yet under her cold exterior, she has not completely lost her humanity; she is compassionate, especially to children—she cannot bring herself to harm them—, and believes the life of an assassin to be loathsome.

Perhaps because of her complex relationship with Zato—her savior, teacher, lover, and enemy—, Millia seems to hold men in low regard, thinking them to be selfish, and is not afraid to voice her biting opinions of them. As for her decision to leave the Guild (which, no matter what, she sees as her home), Millia chose to do so after a greal deal of thinking, as she didn't want to "keep hating what she hated", and the only way out was betraying Zato. No matter her feelings for him, Millia prioritizes her own will above all, and wishes to find happiness. Settling her past, however, has led her to obsession at times.

After leaving the Guild and living among ordinary people, Millia remains a lonely individual, but she has learned to tap into a wider range of human emotion, making her more considerate of others, and more compassionate. She also makes sure the danger that follows her does not spread to others. When faced with a situations she doesn't know how to handle, she will act more like a child than her usual, detached self.

Taken by the Assassin's Guild at young age, Millia has received extensive training that has molded her into a deadly weapon. Having activated the experimental 6th Forbidden Magic Spell "Angra", for which she paid a steep, but unknown price, Millia is able to freely manipulate and control her hair and use it as a lethal weapon. It is alive, even becoming restless in the presence of someone like Slayer, and can be thought of as an equivalent to a Gear or a Forbidden Beast. As a forbidden magic, there is a possibility that she could be corrupted by it, and lose herself to the magic that gave her her power, as it happened with Zato. As it is much more stable than Eddie, this has yet to occur.

Her hair is capable of assuming a myriad of odd shapes such as a sword, a harp, a unicorn, or even wings (which allow her to briefly fly), or to control it even after the strands are no longer attached to her head, as seen in her Iron Maiden technique. Millia's hair shines with golden lights when attacking, and appears able to use magic to create orbs, discs, or spikes to attack her enemy.

entries.name: Millia Rage History
entries.content:
Born in Russia, Millia lost both of her parents to the Crusades at an early age. In 2173, she was found in the ruins of a village and taken in by the Assassin's Guild, now under the recently-appointed leader, Zato-ONE. Taken to be trained as an assassin, Millia activated the 6th Forbidden Spell in 2175, although whether she took the curse freely or if it was forced upon her is unknown. She was then trained to use her hair as a lethal weapon, but Millia wanted no part of such a loathsome life, and tried to commit suicide several times. At the same time, her relationship with Zato evolved from savior, to teacher, to lover, even as she questioned her life as an assassin. Venom, ever protective of Zato, knew of their nights together and treated Millia coldly.

The Guild was then hired to assassinate Duke Dorian Scaburi of Castellia. During the party in honor of King Saltelia I, Millia met Slayer, unaware of his status as the Guild's founder. Later that night, Millia killed the duke in his quarters, but Slayer soon appeared before her. He learned from her that the Guild was not following the code, and asked if Millia was happy with the current organization before disappearing. Due to his meddling, Millia was captured by Leon Mining.

In captivity, Millia realized that she didn't want to die, associating that fate with Zato's path. Slayer then reappeared, and freed her as an "apology". Millia returned to find that Zato—unaware of Slayer's actions—agreed to kill Saltelia I to save her from Mining. When she and Zato reached the infant king's room, Millia struck Zato and fled, snatching the baby away, and informed Venom of his death. Yet, upon hearing that Zato was still alive but surrounded by Mining's forces, they both went to his (and Slayer's) rescue. After Mining's defeat, Millia was forgiven by Zato. Taking responsibility for the baby, she found him a foster home with Johnny's help.

Millia, Zato and Slayer would later cooperate again in the Mount Rosa Operation, but Millia ultimately decided to cut her ties, and leave the Guild. In 2178, secretly working with the IPF to dismantle the Guild and capture Zato in exchange for her acquittal, Millia took part in a high-risk operation led by Zato, during which she was to act alone. She took the opportunity to flee. Her escape threw the assassin into chaos, allowing them to be caught red-handed, and Zato was arrested and imprisoned. Since then, Millia lived on as a fugitive and resorted to killing her pursuers when backed into a corner.

In 2180, Millia hears from one of her unlucky pursuers that Zato has escaped from his dimensional prison and is entering the Second Holy Order Selection Tournament. Millia decides to enter as well. Feeling she will never be free until he is dead, Millia is determined to end his life once and for all, and as the tournament's winner, she could use her wish to end the organization forever. During the tournament, Millia defeats Zato, but is unable to kill him. The blood shed during the tournament releases Justice from her seal, but she is promptly destroyed by Sol Badguy. Millia, for her part, remains a fugitive but from her insistent admirer, who has been following her for six months.

Given the complex feelings—both guilt and dread—she experiences as a result of her battle with Zato in the last tournament, Millia feels it is time to settle the score once and for all. Prior to October 2181,[note 1] Millia informs Venom that his mission regarding Faust's recruitment is meant to keep him away while certain members try to assassinate Zato in a bid for power. She thus convinces Venom to help her find the missing Zato, even as she openly vows to kill him herself.

Unbeknownst to them, Zato has been possessed by Eddie, who is following the scent of a newly-discovered Gear called Dizzy. In one path, Millia finds and fights Eddie, but isn't able to finish him off and he flees. Zato then regains control of his body, asking for forgiveness as he dies, even as Millia implores him not to. In another path, Millia kills Eddie and Zato; Millia's admirer then appears to cheer her up and assures that she will find meaning in life. With Zato's death,[note 2] Eddie remains in control of his host's corpse.

Weeks later, Millia is attacked by I-No, who claims that she "panicked" due to a black beast attacking her. Millia then sets out to find Eddie. In one path, Slayer prevents her from reaching Eddie, and warns that she might end like the dying shadow if she doesn't change the path upon which she treads. In her second path, she bests Slayer and subsequently kills Eddie; fatigued and relieved, Millia returns to her new life. In her third path, I-No is disappointed to see that Millia and the defeated Eddie couldn't kill each other; after defeating the musician, she buries Zato's body, leaving her hair and his blindfold as a memento; despite everything, she thanks him and leaves.

While her revenge against Zato is complete, the Guild is still intact, and Millia is determined to live no matter what. On her way to the Guild's headquarters to settle the matter, Slayer appears to warn her that her hair's forbidden magic might soon corrupt her. In one path, she arrives and attacks Venom; she defeats him but spares his life, making Venom promise that he won't bother her again. Her naivety reminding him of Zato, Venom lets Millia go, making peace with each other. Millia then comes across Eddie, who asks that Millia remember him as he, too, finally dies. Despite finally being free of the guild, a sense of emptiness lingers within Millia as she feels she hasn't had a proper closure.

In her other path, she loses control of her hair and ends up accidentally killing Bridget. Millia's admirer then stabs her, saying it is Millia's fault for never looking at him, and Millia feels content as she dies as herself, not a monster.

Having spent the past few years leading a "normal" life—peaceful days without a care in the world, with smiling neighbors full of joy—, in September 29, 2187, Millia is informed by Venom that Zato has been resurrected by the Conclave. Millia investigates their laboratory, the Opera House, guarded by Venom. They are reunited with Zato, who vows to protect Millia and warns that war is coming. While surprised by his change in personality, Millia is relieved to see him. After they are joined by Slayer, Zato leaves for Japan to investigate, while Millia, Venom and Slayer agree to deliver such information to an appropiate party, King Ky Kiske of Illyria.

Millia, Venom and Slayer are immediately attacked by Bedman, who teleports himself and their unconscious bodies to near Uighur where Faust, Chipp Zanuff and the Jellyfish Pirates are gathered to attack them as well. Bedman backs off, recalled by his ally, when Zato comes to their aid. The Guild's information ultimately reaches Ky on November 1 when Zato manages to meets with him, Sol and President Gabriel at Zepp.

Around November 7, King Daryl hires the Guild as "soldiers", and Millia convenes with the others at Slayer's mansion—all four working to rebuild the Guild. Although she doesn't quite agree with eliminating Bedman for humiliating them, she plays along, trying to find an answer to why she keeps on fighting herself. Before leaving, Venom asks Millia to look after Zato after what is to come. Millia then helps Slayer train; he questions if she really wants to lead a so-called "normal" life, and Millia admits that she doesn't want to be left behind. Privately, Millia acknowledges that normal for her is life in the Guild, but she won't return to a dark void; she will create a place for others to return, and vows to become the next leader of the Guild.

Thanks to Zato's abilities, they locate Bedman, and Slayer engages him in a fight, but Millia stops him before long as they are just testing Zato's accuracy. It is Venom and Robo-Ky who take down Bedman at the same time that Millia, Zato, Slayer and the other assassins participate in the defense of the capitol against the Universal Will's forces. During the fight, Millia and Zato are reminded by Slayer of an old man they met during the Mount Rosa Operation, and Millia orders their men to hold the line, after which tomorrow will have a much different meaning. The battle comes to an end when Ariels is defeated and Jack-O' Valentine merges with Justice.

In the following weeks, King Daryl reinstitutes the Post-War Administration Bureau, hiring the assassins due to their skill at informational warfare. Millia, inheriting the guild's philosophy and beliefs, gathers the guild's former members and reforms the Bureau, becoming its director, to support the Illyrian government. Upon the U.S. agreeing to That Man's involvement at the G4 Summit, they request that all nations involved help with security. Daryl thus calls Millia and Zato as "specialists" for their assistance to investigate the White House's security. At the Illyrian War Room, they inform Daryl and Leo Whitefang of the "black box" they found, and Daryl departs for the summit. Unbeknownst to them, Happy Chaos hacks into their files.

After the summit starts, Leo decides to leave the box be, but then Zato realizes they have been hacked. Meanwhile, Chaos takes Daryl and the other representatives hostage and launches all missiles in the world. Zato manually deactivates the castle's weapons, while the other missiles are deactivated by the dignitaries themselves. Sol then rescues Vernon, who contacts Zepp, and Gabriel establishes a link with the Pentagon and Illyria Castle. After Chaos activates the White House's Tír na nÓg mode, Millia advises everyone on how to approach the aircraft, and oversees its analysis by the Illyrian operators.

Thanks to Leo buying time, Sol and Vernon reach the White House's escape pod, and That Man tricks Chaos into seemingly being ejected. Leo realizes that he is still onboard and tries to alert them, but Chaos uses That Man's Tome of Origin to restore I-No to godhood. As with the rest of the world, Millia witnesses I-No starting a process to grant humanity her same powers, but she is soon defeated by those aboard the White House. In the aftermath, Millia, Zato, Leo and Ky reflect upon the future I-No wanted. Sometime afterward, Zato takes Millia to see Robo-Ky and Venom at his bakery.

entries.name: Nagoriyuki
entries.content:
Nagoriyuki is a character in the Guilty Gear world who makes his first appearance on Guilty Gear -Strive-. He is described as a noble vampire samurai who wields a bloodsucking blade.

Nagoriyuki is a tall, heavily built, dark-skinned man with blue eyes and thick, shoulder-length Dread-locks tied into a ponytail. He wears a white coat with purple lining decorated with silver studs and snaps in the style of a haori, with only his right arm through the sleeve; the back of the jacket is emblazoned with a red kanji 心 (kokoro, heart) and the word "HEART" beneath. This is worn over a simple orange robe cinched at the waist by a red obi and three leather belts, which is likewise half-removed. Beneath this is a long white waist cloth matching his jacket, with several purple and blue straps embroidered with crosses and the phrase "KEEP OUT." He also wears white fingerless gloves, black leggings, and simple gray sandals.

His white mechanical helmet resembles a hannya mask with elongated horns and a rictus grin. In place of eyes and a nose is a featureless white surface marked with the same red kanji that appears on his coat. The helmet can automatically disassemble, retracting behind his head. He also carries a traditional daishou pair of swords sheathed at the hip, with the oodachi locking into its scabbard via a mechanical apparatus in the hilt.

As noble as he is, he is also a kind man, often being willing to provide advice to those he defeats in battle much akin to Slayer, though he often expresses regret and no ill will towards others when it comes to his past being a puppet of Happy Chaos' bidding. Unlike Slayer, he seems to be more active in expressing his desire to help others in spite of having as little worldly-attachments as he does.

Like Slayer, Nagoriyuki is a vampire, and thus endowed with immortality, superhuman speed, extreme durability and godlike strength. Unlike Slayer, however, Nagoriyuki fights using a wakizashi along with a large, magical katana (styled akin to an oodachi or a tachi relative to his own size) that is customized to prevent wounds inflicted by it from healing (as seen in the Story Mode of Strive, where several of his attacks temporarily negated Sol's accelerating regeneration). He can also cause his attacks to send energy waves, with the same effect as being hit with the katana itself, making him dangerous even from afar.

Nagoriyuki also possesses two unique abilities. One of them is being able to sense the weak points of his opponents (which is how he knows the weak point of Happy Chaos). The other, known as Blood Rage, increases his combat abilities even further, while also sharpening his fangs, similar to vampires in other media.

entries.name: Nagoriyuki History
entries.content:
Nagoriyuki is a Nightless samurai and the retainer of a man named Kazusanosuke. During the Crusades, he encountered Happy Chaos, who used his powers to force him to do his bidding. At some point after these events, Nagoriyuki paid a vast sum to rent out the basement level of a luxurious high-rise in Illyria, where he spent the next several decades in meditative hibernation.

Guilty Gear -Strive-
Nagoriyuki is found and awakened by Chaos, who once again uses his binding magic to force him to be his bodyguard, since he is the only person who knows his weakness. During the ensuing events he is forced to fight on behalf of Chaos and I-No, and Chaos also copies the unique properties of his blade to create bullets that slows health regeneration's speed for short periods. His ability to use Gamma Blade surprises Chipp Zanuff during their first encounter.

Through these battles, he develops a rivalry with Sol Badguy, telling him his flaws in battle as they fight. However, in their final battle, Nagoriyuki praises him and breaks free of Chaos's control, allowing Sol to defeat him, but sadly have no time to ask him about Chaos' weakness, as Sol is in hurry with US President Vernon E. Groubitz, and the Gear Maker Asuka R. Kreutz to escape from Chaos, but instead, tricking him into being trapped inside the air ship White House's PEOC escape pod and got rid of him.

However, when the real Chaos is revealed to still be aboard the airship, and uses the Tome of Origin which fused with Asuka to fuse the former with I-No, to restore the witch's full godlike power, Nagoriyuki is properly freed from Chaos' control.

In the final battle against a godlike I-No, he returns to help Sol (now simply a 'human' named Frederick Bulsara), Ky and Axl Low find and expose her weak point, allowing Sol to destroy her with his Outrage cannon. With Chaos and I-No gone, Nagoriyuki's whereabouts are unknown.

entries.name: Order-Sol
entries.content:
Order-Sol is a character in the Guilty Gear world. He is a past version of Sol Badguy back when he was enlisted with the Sacred Order of Holy Knights towards the end of the Crusades, circa 2172 AD.

Physically, he looks the same as his current self: long, spiky brown hair held together by his trademark headband with the "Rock You" inscription, a muscular build, and eyes that are usually brown in color, but sometimes turn gold with slit pupils.

His outfit is the standard, red based version of the Sacred Order of Holy Knights uniform, fastened together with his belt plate inscribed with the word "FREE", also wearing a tight sleeved black and white undershirt. Order-Sol's design also contains white based with black finger gloves. He wears red boots that are extremely similar to those he wears in Guilty Gear and Guilty Gear X.

Order-Sol's personality is similar as the present one: both being sullen and unrefined, speaking to others only when absolutely necessary. Despite being the same person, Sol seems more irritable and bitter, but is not as openly rude to others as the present Sol via likely keeping to himself more around professional company.

Within the Order's organization, heeding the word "FREE" as his motto, Sol is a lone wolf and rarely works alongside others, with his missions being mostly guerrilla-style attacks, and disobeying direct orders so as to kill Gears on his own as he always has. Despite being acknowledged as a great fighter, many of his fellow knights are said to bear him "little more than ill will". Nevertheless, perhaps because of his skill or his close ties to Kliff and Ky, many refer to Sol as "sir" despite Sol—presumably—not being a ranking officer.

Sol's weapon of choice during this time is a rugged, improvised weapon that is nonetheless quite effective against multiple opponents. Because of the difficulty in channeling his powers, he needs to concentrate in order to release their full potential. Of a somewhat sluggish movement than his present self, Order-Sol uses a more all-out fighting style with a majority of his attacks being prototypes for his future moves, to be refined upon obtaining the Fireseal.

Because of how more refined-yet-toned-down (out of being less inclined and jaded over the years) his present-self is, Order-Sol's fighting style can be compared more as "all-over-the-place", involving more roughness and desperation in his motions/actions.

entries.name: Order-Sol History
entries.content:
In 2172, rumors of Sol as an immensely skilled lone-wolf bounty hunter reached Kliff Undersn, the old commander of the Sacred Order of Holy Knights. Having been saved by Sol in his youth, Kliff was interested in recruiting him, and spared no means in finding Sol. During the meeting, Kliff invited Sol to become a member, and told Sol a rumor about a "prodigy swordsman". Sol couldn't care less about that, but joined the Holy Order to obtain information on Gears.

Sol soon met the "prodigy", Ky Kiske, whose skills on the battlefield surpassed all of his expectations, and thought the young knight to be a "killing machine".
